n6808a24d9bca: As elsewhere in the world, archaeological records in eastern Africa show that long environmental variabilities shaped the emergence and development of farming economies. Marine sediments and isotopic data indicate alternating humid and arid phases that coincide with the reorganization of settlements, establishment of agricultural landscapes, and the generation of new subsistence practices during the later Holocene. Strengthened monsoons during the African Humid Period (13,050–3050 BCE) produced environments that enabled human mobility, likely experimentation with plants, and the dispersal of early herders through the Rift Valley and the Horn of Africa. Archaeological, archaeobotanical, isotopic, and other data from sites in the Rift Valley, Lake Victoria, and elsewhere indicate varied and gradual transitions from foraging to mixed farming, shaped by microenvironments, altitude, and intercommunity exchanges. Case studies of farming systems developed over the last 2,000 years demonstrate innovative forms of resilient landscape engineering and complex social management. We suggest that the equity and collective stewardship attested by this record offer valuable analogues for contemporary climate adaptation in the Anthropocene.
n1ac9129e894b: This reflection on my years in linguistic anthropology also includes the broader sociohistorical transformations of which I have been a part. The Cold War and its aftermath were the backdrop against which we learned and taught. As a child migrant to the United States from the Soviet region, I became fascinated by the intersection of political relationships and linguistic practices. At the same time, linguistic anthropology was starting to navigate between theories of political economy and the analysis of speaking as action-in-events. Within that endeavor, I have studied conceptual questions about multilingualism and the workings of language ideology as well as questions about sign phenomena in constructing gender, sociocultural differentiation, scaling, and translation. My scholarly path has depended on the generous, inspiring influence of mentors, colleagues, and students, individually and in the many seminars and study groups we have formed together. Working now on analyzing authoritarian regimes, I see with alarm their effects on public expression, safety, and protest, echoing my earliest memories of repression.
nc37ea52f64d4: How anthropologists have invoked and conceptualized anxiety reflects the development of new ways of relating selfhood, subjectivity, and the sociopolitical to each other. This article examines the recent development of anthropological frameworks of anxiety in the context of the rising prevalence of and interest in anxiety. Since its inception in modern social theory, anxiety has functioned as a commentary on people's relation to risk, precarity, and emerging forms of capitalism. Early anthropological approaches to anxiety relied extensively on psychological theories that focused on the emotions at an individual level. Although they framed anxiety as a social condition in addition to an inner one, they were still beholden to the politics and ethics of the sovereign subject and dichotomies between self and society, individual and collective, and citizen and state. By framing anxiety as a social practice and relation, contemporary anthropologists are now redefining anxiety's role in political-economic transformations from a passive reflection of widespread uncertainty and insecurity to an agentive constituent of politics itself.
nb7d681096d2b: A review of the anthropological literature motivates an expansive definition of the therapeutic as practices that have or are purported to have salubrious effects on at least one of the parties involved. Those effects could be on the psychic or spiritual state of participants (i.e., what one is or has), on how they make sense of their state or circumstances (i.e., how one sees, feels, understands, or knows), and/or on their behavior (i.e., what one does and says, how, and to what effect). The idea that the therapeutic is invariably a matter of communicative practice is a premise of this review, which addresses ( a ) the diversity and distinctiveness of therapies as multimodal genres; ( b ) the therapeutic distillation of cultural values, projects, and ideals; ( c ) the epistemic and interpretive challenges of therapeutic communication, particularly relative to politically loaded questions of mediation; and ( d ) the scaling of the therapeutic as a kind of communication by way of communication.
n86ff13de8d4a: This article provides an overview of experimental anthropology, arguing that, from its inception, anthropology has operated as a form of experimental inquiry aimed at producing a surplus of data, relations, and sensations. We explore this notion through a tripartite heuristic for understanding how anthropological creativity draws on methods from the natural sciences as well as from art and design: ( a ) experience-based experimentation, ( b ) the adoption of scientific protocols and instruments, and ( c ) experimentation with and through models. Despite the apparent diversity of contemporary approaches, efforts to reimagine experimentalism in anthropology can still be understood through this heuristic. We revisit it in reverse order, arguing, first, that modeling now takes place through prototypes, games, devices, and other relational infrastructures; second, that apparatus-based experimentation has opened new possibilities for sensory enrichment; and finally, that anthropological practice itself emerges as a radical venture that expands conceptual, physical, and existential boundaries, with ethnographic inquiry relentlessly generating excess data.
n727fc55c624a: Tactile sensing provides robots with direct access to physical interactions at the contact interface, making it a critical modality for robust and dexterous manipulation. Over the past several decades, tactile-based manipulation research has evolved from mechanics-driven approaches, which explicitly interpret tactile signals through contact mechanics and task-specific reasoning, to data-driven approaches that learn tactile representations and manipulation policies directly from data. This article reviews the development of tactile-based manipulation from these two complementary perspectives. We first introduce the fundamentals of tactile sensing and then review, from a mechanics-driven perspective, how those signals form manipulation-relevant state representations and subsequently influence the robot action. We then examine the recent advances in data-driven tactile manipulation, covering imitation learning, reinforcement learning, vision–language–action models, and predictive models. Finally, we discuss open challenges and future opportunities toward scalable, generalizable, and robust tactile-enabled robotic systems.
ncfa127a7cc72: Forest insects worldwide face changing environments within a given year and across multiple years. Therefore, insects must match their life cycles with critical resources to maximize fitness and survival. A key strategy for life-cycle synchronization is entry into a special form of dormancy, called diapause. Diapause affects multiple life-history traits, including development, reproduction, movement, stress resistance, and energy storage. This review provides an overview and discussion of diapause expression for forest insects, focusing on ecologically and economically relevant plant-feeding species and highlighting specific, diapause-related features of forests. Diapause regulation and expression are highly variable across species and mainly help overcome unfavorable periods, synchronize life cycles with host trees and predators, and respond to scarce or irregular resources. Changing climatic conditions have direct and indirect effects on forest insect diapause, including temperature stress, energetic stress, and phenological mismatches. Knowledge of diapause regulation is essential for practical forestry to coordinate and evaluate management measures.
n263ea53659a4: In brood-site pollination mutualisms (BSPMs), insect pollinators breed within the plants that they pollinate. Organisms involved in BSPMs show adaptations in life-history strategies and life cycles. BSPM plants are monoecious or dioecious, or have bisexual flowers; are monocot or dicot; and are angiosperms or gymnosperms. All plants are perennial, mostly iteroparous, while a few are semelparous. The highly specific pollinators are mostly small-sized wasps, micromoths, thrips, fungus gnats, flower weevils, beetles, and gall midges. Most BSPMs involve ovule/seed parasites, while larvae also consume pollen, other floral tissues, and fungi. Active pollination occurs only in ovule/seed parasites, accompanied by special pollen-deposition structures and reduced pollen:ovule ratios. Quiescent stages involving egg, larval, prepupal, and pupal diapause enable synchrony with plant reproduction. Prolonged flower longevity enables the completion of larval growth. Haplodiploidy via arrhenotoky or paternal genome elimination often occurs. Many brood sites constitute mating arenas and impose restriction of mating opportunities.
nddc746c4812f: Candida ( Candidozyma ) auris is a pathogenic fungus first identified in a patient in 2009. Prior to this clinical finding, C. auris was unknown, with its closest relative being the marine-dwelling Candida haemulonii. Infections are increasing annually, predominately impacting hospital patients due to durable biofilms on medical devices and antimicrobial resistance. Perplexingly, the fungus arose nearly simultaneously across the globe in independent disease emergences from six genetically distinct clades. The C. auris clades mostly diverged from one another 5,000–10,000 years ago, during a period when global temperatures and sea levels rose and coastal wetlands flourished. Within the past 200–300 years, a new wave of rapid divergence occurred within each clade. This corresponds to industrialization, urbanization, global warming, and the widespread wetland destruction. Environmental stressors, including heat, are hypothesized to have driven mutations and stress resistance. These may not only help C. auris withstand a changing climate but also help it thrive within mammalian hosts.
nc2e699c45070: Fragile X syndrome (FXS) is caused by CGG repeat expansion in FMR1 , leading to gene silencing and loss of fragile X messenger ribonucleoprotein (FMRP). As the most common inherited cause of intellectual disability and a leading monogenic cause of autism spectrum disorder, FXS has provided an unusually tractable framework for linking a single-gene defect to abnormalities in RNA regulation, synaptic development, circuit function, and behavior. In this review, we synthesize current understanding of FMRP function, dysregulated signaling pathways, synaptic and network phenotypes, and emerging contributions from glial and human organoid models. We also evaluate therapeutic efforts, emphasizing lessons from failed targeted trials, the constraints imposed by critical developmental periods, and newer strategies aimed at restoring FMR1 itself. We argue that future progress will depend on earlier intervention, biologically informed patient stratification, and objective measures of target engagement and circuit response.
n4e194ecc00f6: Dinosaurs dominated terrestrial ecosystems for more than 160 million years under fluctuating atmospheric conditions that profoundly shaped their cardiovascular physiology. Evidence from phylogenetic bracketing, fossil morphology, and comparative models with crocodilians, birds, and mammals suggests that many dinosaurs possessed a fully separated four-chambered heart capable of sustaining high systemic pressures and efficient oxygen (O 2 ) transport. In sauropods, extreme vertical distances between the heart and brain required arterial pressures exceeding those of any extant vertebrate, raising questions about cardiac structure, ventricular wall stress, and vascular adaptations. Oxygen transport was further modulated by atmospheric O 2 variability across the Mesozoic and therefore sauropods likely managed these changes by shaping their hemoglobin affinity, capillary density, respiratory system, and Bohr and Haldane effects. Mitochondrial density, redox balance, and the regulation of reactive species such as nitric oxide and hydrogen sulfide may have already underpinned thermoregulation, metabolic reprogramming, and tissue energetics. By integrating paleophysiology with modern comparative physiology, this review discusses how informed speculations on sauropods cardiovascular biology may be used to improve our understanding of endothermy, gigantism, and adaptive strategies in variations of O 2 /carbon dioxide environments. We posit that the necessary adaptations of the heart, microcirculation, and pressure–volume relations are relevant for understanding extreme physiology and, in some cases, human cardiovascular disease. This review synthesizes current knowledge on sauropods cardiovascular physiology, focusing on cardiac function, vascular architecture, O 2 transport, and whole-organism integration.
ne2e3bf4ba4c6: Cellular senescence is a stress-responsive cell fate characterized by stable growth arrest and acquisition of a proinflammatory senescence-associated secretory phenotype. Senescent cells accumulate with advancing age and contribute to dysfunction and disease across multiple organ systems. In skeletal muscle (SkM), emerging evidence indicates that senescence arises across diverse cell populations that collectively reshape the SkM niche. Through the SASP and altered intercellular signaling, senescent cells promote chronic inflammation, fibrosis, impaired regeneration, and metabolic dysfunction that contribute to SkM loss, SkM weakness, functional decline, and frailty. This review synthesizes current knowledge of the molecular drivers, hallmarks, and cellular origins of senescence within SkM and highlights the physiological consequences that extend from the cellular to the organismal level. We also discuss emerging senotherapeutic strategies that hold promise for optimizing SkM health and function with aging and disease.
n4a7543508958: The capacity to re-experience a moment from one's past, known as episodic memory, is critical for our ability to navigate the present and plan for the future. This article reviews and synthesizes over a half century of behavioral and neuroscientific research that has shaped our understanding of how we remember past events. This work has revealed complementary truths about episodic memory: Episodic memories seem to be based on traces of experience, carrying objective information about specific moments in time, and on imaginative reconstructions, built on a scaffold of prior knowledge. We propose that the tension between these perspectives can be reconciled by conceptualizing episodic memory not as a readout from a static memory system but as the outcome of two neurocognitive modes— a generative mode that facilitates schema-based inference and prediction, and a contextual mode that binds memories to context-specific anchor points. Drawing from experimental findings and computational models, we describe how multiple memory modes arise from dynamic cortico-hippocampal interactions, allowing episodic memory to be at once precise and constructive.
nf0f6e9d46b44: Introduction Movement behaviours (sleep, sedentary behaviour, and physical activity) influence numerous health outcomes in children, including their social-emotional development. The optimal 24-hour movement behaviour composition for positive social-emotional development is unknown. The purpose of this study was to determine the movement behaviour composition across the 24-hour day associated with desired social-emotional functioning in the early years. Methods This cross-sectional analysis included 560 children aged 1.2–2.9 years and 1,500 children aged 3.0–4.9 years from the Sleep and Activity Database (SADEY) for the Early Years study. Sedentary behaviour (SED), light physical activity (LPA), and moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA) were measured using ActiGraph accelerometers. Sleep duration was assessed using parent reports. Children social-emotional functioning was measured using the five domains of the Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire (SDQ), a widely used screening instrument of children’s behaviours, emotions, and relationships across five domains (emotional problems, conduct problems, hyperactivity, peer problems, and prosocial behaviour). Compositional data analyses were used to estimate the 24-hour movement behaviour compositions associated with optimal scores for each of the SDQ domain z-scores and all five domains combined (the Goldilocks day). Results The movement behaviour composition was significantly associated with all five SDQ domains (all p < .01). For 1–2-year-olds, the Goldilocks day consisted of 12 h 12 min of sleep, 4 h 36 min of SED, 5 h 48 min of LPA, and 1h 24 min of MVPA. For 3–4-year-olds, it consisted of 12 h 08 min of sleep, 4 h 27 min of SED, 5 h 49 min of LPA, and 1 h 36 min of MVPA. Conclusion The duration of total physical activity and MVPA associated with more favourable social-emotional functioning exceeded the minimum levels specified in the current 24-hour Movement Guidelines. These findings should not be interpreted as behavioural recommendations but rather as movement behaviour patterns associated with more favourable outcomes within this study population.
nd26bee347ee3: Researchers have long studied allostatic (over)load as an estimated measure of individual cumulative stress over a lifetime. Often called the overall ‘wear and tear’ from social and environmental stressors, allostatic (over)load shows promise as a practical indicator of general health trends in community settings. This data processing workflow aims to document our overall approach and reasoning when calculating allostatic (over)load for data analysis and knowledge sharing. The included repository features an R script for generating datasets using this workflow from the following data sources: All of Us Research Program data repository. Health and Retirement Study (HRS). National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES). Our allostatic (over)load measurement process, along with the linked repository, provides a reproducible workflow to process secondary data and offers insights into protocol-driven measurement practices in community environments.
n6492c8cf0839: Aiming to balance localization accuracy, computational complexity, and robustness under low-SNR conditions in three-dimensional interference source localization, this paper proposes an efficient method combining frequency-domain covariance matrix reconstruction (FDCMR) and adaptive voxel iteration. First, the proposed method employs FDCMR-based direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation for multi-station coarse localization and uses the intersection of direction cones to substantially compress the global search region. An adaptive voxel iteration with exponentially decreasing resolution is then performed within the compressed region for position refinement. Complexity analysis shows that the proposed method replaces exhaustive direct position determination (DPD) evaluation over the global search region with a bounded number of evaluations in a local adaptive voxel region, thereby substantially reducing the spatial-search complexity. Under the considered 2000 m × 2000 m × 2000 m search region with a 5 m spatial resolution, the number of DPD objective-function evaluations is reduced by approximately five orders of magnitude compared with conventional global DPD, while a localization accuracy of about 5 m is maintained at an SNR of 20 dB. At an SNR of −15 dB, the localization error is reduced by approximately 70% compared with the fixed-grid DPD method. These results demonstrate that the proposed method provides an effective balance between localization accuracy, computational efficiency, and low-SNR robustness.
n1d2b7014e8ab: The Artificial Potential Field (APF) method is widely used in robot path planning due to its simplicity and computational efficiency. However, it is well known to suffer from the local minima problem, where the resultant force acting on the robot becomes zero at non-goal configurations, leading to motion stagnation in cluttered environments. This paper proposes an optimization-based waypoint generation framework to address the local minima issue in APF navigation while ensuring explicit collision avoidance. When the direct path between the robot and the target is infeasible due to obstacle interference, intermediate waypoints are generated by solving a constrained optimization problem that guides the robot along a locally defined reference direction while enforcing obstacle clearance constraints for each path segment. Unlike conventional APF modifications that rely on artificial perturbation forces or random escape strategies, the proposed method constructs collision-free intermediate waypoints through finite candidate evaluation and explicit segment-wise collision checking, enabling the robot to avoid obstacles and overcome local-minima while preserving goal-directed motion and ensuring convergence to the target. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is validated through numerical simulations on two robotic platforms, namely a point-mass robot and a wheelchair-type robotic model. The results demonstrate that the method successfully resolves local minima situations, ensures collision-free motion, and consistently guides the robots to their target locations in complex environments. Furthermore, the framework is general and can be applied to different robotic systems.
neb2692231f9d: by Md. Nuruzzaman Khan Background Reproductive coercion is an under-recognised form of violence against women and is not routinely captured by standard measures of intimate partner violence, which commonly focus on physical, sexual, and emotional violence. This study examined the association between reproductive coercion and these measured forms of intimate partner violence and estimated the proportion of women who reported reproductive coercion without reporting any of the physical, sexual, or emotional violence items included in the survey. Methods We analysed nationally representative data from 24,951 ever-married women, including 22,161 currently married women, in the Bangladesh Violence Against Women Survey 2024. Outcomes were physical, sexual, emotional, and any conventional IPV, assessed in the past 12 months among currently married women and over the lifetime among ever-married women. Exposures were reproductive coercion pattern and contraceptive coercion typology. Survey-weighted Poisson regression with robust standard errors estimated adjusted prevalence ratios (aPRs) with 95% CIs for associations with conventional IPV. Survey-weighted logistic regression examined factors associated with reproductive coercion without reported conventional IPV and was considered exploratory because of the small number of events. Survey-weighted prevalence estimates were applied to 2022 census population counts to derive population estimates with 95% uncertainty intervals (UIs). Findings In the past 12 months, 27.30% of currently married women reported conventional IPV and 3.59% reported reproductive coercion; corresponding lifetime prevalences among ever-married women were 60.40% and 9.25%. Including reproductive coercion increased the prevalence of any reported abuse to 28.61% and 61.18%, respectively. Reproductive coercion was associated with a higher prevalence of each form of conventional IPV, with the largest aPRs among women reporting multiple forms of reproductive coercion. Reproductive coercion without reported conventional IPV was reported by 1.31% (95% CI 1.08–1.59) of currently married women in the past 12 months and 0.78% (0.60–1.01) of ever-married women over the lifetime, corresponding to approximately 645,483 (95% UI 532,154–783,449) and 437,414 (337,106–567,462) women, respectively. Interpretation Reproductive coercion captures a dimension of violence against women that is only partly reflected in conventional IPV measures. Women reporting reproductive coercion without conventional IPV might have experienced unmeasured or unreported violence; therefore, this group indicates a measurement gap rather than absence of other abuse. Including validated reproductive coercion measures in national violence surveys could improve evidence for health, legal, and social support responses.
nd0e5411458ab: Introduction Long COVID is a complex pathophysiological condition linked to a heterogenous symptom profile. Dysregulation of 1) immunological and inflammatory responses, 2) endothelial/vascular function, and 3) metabolic and clotting processes have been identified; however, there remains a lack of clinically validated diagnostic biomarkers. The study aim was to investigate dysregulation of cytokines, chemokines and growth factors in confirmed Long COVID cases grouped by disease severity. Methods One-hundred-and-twenty-seven participants provided venous blood samples for cytokine profiling utilising Luminex assays. Participants were grouped into those with no knowledge of SARS-CoV-2 infection (n = 21), acute infection within 3-months (n = 22), spontaneous resolvers (>3-months, n = 21) and those with confirmed Long COVID (n = 63). Long COVID severity was grouped according to the post-COVID-19 functional status (PCFS) and defined as those with negligible (4A; n = 9), mild (4B; n = 20), moderate (4C; n = 24), and severe limitations (4D; n = 10). Cytokines were assessed for normality using Shapiro-Wilk tests and differences measured between groups using Kruskal-Wallis tests. Pairwise correlation and principal component analysis were performed. Results Interleukin-12 (p40/p70) was 22% greater in the Long COVID group (Median [IQR]: 58 [49] pg/mL, p = 0.046) and 30% greater in the acutely infected group (64 [36] pg/mL; p = 0.039) against non-infected controls (45 [25] pg/mL). Following PCFS classification, fibroblast growth factor-basic was 25% lower in Long COVID 4B versus spontaneous resolvers (24 [7] vs. 32 [24] pg/mL; p = 0.025). Pairwise correlation differences demonstrated that three Long COVID subgroups had strong, positive associations between cytokines when compared to non-infected controls; however, PCA was unable to determine any coordinated cytokine variation that was group specific. Discussion and conclusions Elevated interleukin-12 (p40/p70) and reduced basic fibroblast growth factor suggest persistent immune activation and possible subgroup-specific Long COVID; however, these findings were marginally significant and exploratory. A coordinated but partial immunological/inflammatory profile may exist in some of those with Long COVID, suggesting a rationale for subgrouping upon a biological, rather than self-report basis but larger longitudinal studies are required to confirm this hypothesis.
n33a70f997b0c: Hearing loss has been identified as a modifiable risk factor for cognitive decline and dementia, although most of the evidence is derived from studies in older adults. Identifying such cognitive impairment in midlife is crucial, as it serves as a baseline for understanding changes in cognitive abilities that occur later in life. The present study aimed to compare the cognitive performance of age- and socioeconomic status-matched middle-aged adults with normal hearing and those with untreated hearing loss. This study included 48 participants aged 40–65 years, comprising 24 adults with normal hearing and 24 with untreated hearing loss. Among the latter participants, 9 had unilateral loss and 15 had bilateral loss. The cognitive evaluation involved assessing memory (forward and backward digit span and contextual memory test), attention via the Go/No-Go task, and executive function via the letter and category fluency tasks. Results showed that adults with untreated hearing loss performed significantly poorer on all the cognitive tasks compared to their normal-hearing counterparts. Large effect sizes were observed for memory tasks, the category fluency task and Go/No-Go accuracy, and a moderate effect size for the letter fluency tasks. Furthermore, multivariate linear regression analysis demonstrated that better-ear pure-tone thresholds independently predicted cognitive performance, but not age or education. These findings provide preliminary evidence on the association between untreated hearing loss and cognitive performance in middle age. However, considering the modest sample size and cross-sectional study design, longitudinal studies are needed to determine the temporal relationship between hearing loss and cognitive changes.
n8edad6c18c76: This study compares four modeling methods, namely quadratic regression (QR), Lasso, random forest (RF), and multilayer perceptron (MLP), to determine the optimal solid density for four-color offset printing. Based on 110 valid samples for each ink color, random 5-fold cross-validation (CV) and paired t-tests were employed to evaluate model predictive accuracy (R2, RMSE) and the stability of the estimated optimal solid density (CV%). Under random 5-fold CV, non-parametric approaches (RF and MLP) outperformed parametric counterparts (QR and Lasso) for black, cyan, and magenta inks, and MLP yielded the optimal performance for yellow ink (R2 = 0.9770). Pairwise statistical tests showed no significant differences between RF and MLP for black, cyan, and magenta inks (p > 0.05), while MLP was statistically superior for yellow ink under random 5-fold CV (p = 0.0296). However, this ranking cannot be generalized to blocked cross‑validation (blocked‑CV). Two blocked‑CV strategies, temporal-block and spatial-block CV, were further implemented to mitigate data leakage arising from high lag-1 autocorrelation (0.96–0.98) in sequentially collected process data. Under blocked-CV, mean R2 values were negative across most models and ink colors, limiting the interpretability of inter-model rankings. While surfaces fitted under random 5-fold CV revealed nonlinear features including broad high-quality plateaus for cyan and magenta inks and multi-peak patterns for yellow ink, such features require cautious physical interpretation given validation-strategy dependence. Despite substantial drops in predictive performance metrics under blocked-CV, the estimated optimal solid densities were insensitive to the fold structure, with deviations ranging from 0.0034 to 0.0152 across all four ink colors. The recommended optimal solid densities are 1.67 (RF) for black ink, 1.44 (RF) for cyan ink, 1.42 (RF) for magenta ink, and 0.99 (MLP) for yellow ink. This study shows that although predictive performance metrics are highly sensitive to the validation strategies, the estimated optimal solid densities are insensitive to the fold structure examined here. This consistency is dataset‑specific and does not by itself establish out‑of‑sample validity under different printing conditions. For offset printing process optimization, the stability of the estimated optimal solid density offers greater practical engineering value than raw predictive performance or model ranking consistency.
n8e044b68623e: by Anqi Hu, Jinyuan Liu, Peng Chen, Kuixing Yang, Fan Xu, Gai Luo, Jiali Zhang, Mengnan He
n9bbcb08b0313: Background The Depression, Anxiety and Stress Scale for Youth (DASS-Y) has been validated in several countries, but its measurement equivalence between Middle Eastern and East Asian adolescents remains untested, and prior validations primarily relied on single analytic approaches without examining complex factor structures or brief screening forms. This study evaluated the DASS-Y in Lebanese adolescents enduring sociopolitical strain and Chinese adolescents under comparatively stable conditions. Methods The sample comprised 758 Lebanese (M age = 15.95, SD = 1.78; 63.2% female) and 1,062 Chinese adolescents (M age = 16.83, SD = 0.59; 47.5% female). Psychometric properties were examined using confirmatory factor analysis, exploratory structural equation modeling (ESEM), and bifactor variants of both. Differential item functioning was assessed using Rasch analysis. Reliability was indexed by composite reliability (CR), average variance extracted (AVE), and person separation reliability. Results Lebanese adolescents showed a largely unidimensional pattern, whereas an ESEM solution better represented the Chinese data. Reliability was strong in both samples (subscale CR = 0.91 to 0.95, AVE = 0.58 to 0.71, person separation reliability = 0.79 to 0.85; total CR = 0.97 in both samples; total AVE = 0.63 for the Lebanese and 0.61 for the Chinese sample). Several items, mainly in the stress subscale, functioned non-equivalently across samples. The 12-item short form performed comparably (subscale CR = 0.88 to 0.92, AVE = 0.65 to 0.73; total CR = 0.96 and 0.94; total AVE = 0.64 and 0.57, respectively). Conclusions Lebanese adolescents’ responses reflected a unitary distress construct, whereas Chinese adolescents’ responses showed greater differentiation among depression, anxiety, and stress, though a general distress factor remained dominant in both samples. Reliability was high throughout, so this divergence is structural rather than a matter of measurement precision. The 12-item form offers a practical screening option pending further cross-national confirmation.
nbfb95b123758: Introduction Nutritional challenges are a global public health concern, especially among children under five in sub-Saharan African countries. The coexistence of an overweight/obese mother and an underweight child in the same household is recognized as a dual burden of malnutrition (DBM). This study estimated the prevalence, identified associated factors, and assessed socioeconomic inequalities in DBM among mother-child dyads in Mozambique. Methods We used nationally representative, cross-sectional data from the Mozambique Demographic and Health Survey 2022–2023 (n = 3,605 mother-child dyads). Child undernutrition and maternal BMI status were calculated using the World Health Organisation (WHO) standard guidelines. The outcome variable, DBM, was defined as the presence of child undernutrition condition (stunting, wasting or underweight) with corresponding maternal overweight/obesity. Multivariable binary logistic regression, Erreygers’s concentration index, and concentration curve analyses were performed, accounting for the complex survey design, to determine associated factors and social inequalities. Results The prevalence of DBM was 5.5% [95% CI: 4.6, 6.6]. Mothers aged ≥ 34 years [aOR (95% CI): 4.01(1.44, 11.14); p < 0.05] and mothers with four or more children [aOR (95% CI): 2.68(1.29, 5.57); p < 0.05] had higher odds of DBM. Rural residence and using unimproved toilet facilities (latter an indicator) were also significantly associated with DBM. Additionally, maternal age modified the association between women’s empowerment and mother-child DBM. Women aged 15–19 years at the lowest and highest empowerment levels were more likely to experience DBM than women 20 years or older. A positive and statistically significant concentration index indicates that wealth-related inequalities exist, with DBM more concentrated among wealthier mother-child dyads. Conclusion Our study highlights the occurrence of household-level DBM in Mozambique. These findings emphasize the need for targeted interventions addressing social and economic inequalities, including poor sanitation, a marker of broader household deprivation. Prioritizing integrated maternal-child nutrition interventions within national strategies is essential to improving equity in nutrition and health outcomes.
nc0cbb56996ae: Background The International Trauma Questionnaire (ITQ) is a widely used self-report measure of PTSD and Complex PTSD (CPTSD). ‘Clinical checks’ – brief follow up questions verifying respondent comprehension of the symptom item – have recently been developed for the ITQ to reduce false-positive diagnostic cases. This study tested whether the ITQ with clinical checks generates psychometrically sound scores and adds clinically relevant information to standard symptom assessment. Methods Data (N = 5,070) were collected using quota-based sampling procedures from adults living in five European countries (Czech Republic, Poland, Hungary, Romania, and Slovakia). Results Overall, 82.2% of respondents were trauma-exposed, and 19.2% met diagnostic requirements for PTSD (7.2%) or CPTSD (12.0%) on the standard ITQ. With clinical checks, these fell to 9.8% overall, 3.9% for PTSD, and 5.9% for CPTSD. The ITQ with clinical checks produced scores with excellent factorial validity, internal reliability, and latent classes corresponding to PTSD and CPTSD. Associations with clinically relevant variables including suicidality and anxiety-depression symptoms were stronger with than without the clinical checks. Females, those with more extensive trauma histories, and higher concurrent anxiety-depression symptoms were more likely to retain than lose their diagnostic status when the clinical checks were used. Conclusions The ITQ with clinical checks generated scores with excellent psychometric properties, captured additional clinically relevant information, and yielded more plausible prevalence estimates compared to the standard ITQ scores. The potential value and limitations of using clinical checks in self-report questionnaires are discussed.
n5bc1a1147ce0: by Adrián F. Hernández-Borda, María P. Rojas-Sepúlveda, Hanz Y. Ramírez-Gómez Photons and optical circuits are among the most promising platforms for implementation of quantum technologies, including quantum computing and quantum cryptography. For entanglement-based quantum key distribution, on-demand sources of highly entangled photon pairs are essential, and semiconductor quantum dots have emerged as prominent candidates to satisfy the necessary conditions of brightness and fidelity. However, in most cases the photon pair emitted by these sources is an anomalous Bell state whose relative phase and purity are non-ideal, and then, their suitability for distributing secret keys must be assessed. This work studies the performance of the quantum key distribution protocol E91, under the influence of three elements: the phase in the input state, the impurity of such a state, and the relative directions of the polarization analyzers. We derive analytical expressions for the minimum quantum bit error rate and the Bell’s parameter, and validate them by using quantum computational tools. Our results show that the performance of the quantum transmission is highly impacted by the phase and purity of the entangled input states, and that such an impact may be modulated through the orientation of the polarizers. These findings provide important insight for the scalable implementation of quantum key distribution protocols with realistic entanglement sources.
n74dc9085d074: Purpose The recent James Lind Alliance (JLA) Priority Setting Partnership (PSP) on ‘the problematic knee replacement’ highlighted implant selection at revision knee arthroplasty (rTKA) as a ‘Top 10’ research priority. The aims of this scoping review are to map the evidence for the implants used at first-time elective aseptic rTKA, to identify gaps in the evidence-base, and to provide recommendations for future research. Methods A scoping review was conducted in accordance with the Arksey and O’Malley framework and the Joanna Briggs Institute Manual for Evidence Synthesis, and reported according to the PRISMA extension for Scoping Reviews. A comprehensive search of MEDLINE, Embase, CINAHL, CDSR, CENTRAL, DARE, HTA, SCI, PROSPERO and KSR Evidence was conducted on 17th August 2026, covering studies published between 2000 and 2026. Annual reports of 17 national joint replacement registries (NJRRs) were also sought. The review was registered on the Open Science Framework (https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/SD49V). Results Following deduplication, 7,096 research articles and 155 NJRR reports were identified. After applying eligibility criteria, 121 research articles and six NJRR reports were included. Twenty-two studies (18%) had cohorts clearly defined as exclusively comprising first-time elective aseptic rTKA procedures. The evidence consisted mostly of retrospective case series (45/121, 37%) and retrospective comparative studies (41/121, 34%). Most evidence was Level IV (48/121, 40%) or Level III (46/121, 38%) with no Level I evidence identified. Approximately half the studies were from the United States (58/102, 48%). Five studies (4%) reported mean or median follow up ≥10 years. A map of the evidence, tabulated by five key themes, is presented. Conclusions There is a lack of high-level comparative evidence to support implant selection at first-time elective aseptic rTKA. Future research should focus on more clinically homogeneous cohorts and compare outcomes associated with cemented versus hybrid/cementless stems, constraint levels, and metaphyseal fixation devices.
ne1fd2d2a4845: by Md. Emon Prodhan, Ashraful Alam, Sajida Subha, Faizul Islam, Mohd. Al Amin, Mohammad Nayeem Hasan, Mohammad Anamul Haque, Md Jamal Uddin Primary school dropout is a serious concern worldwide. In Bangladesh, primary education is strongly shaped by the home learning environment. This study aimed to investigate the associations between the dropout of primary school children and the learning environment at home as well as the associated risk factors by analyzing cross-sectional data from the 2019 Multiple Indicator Cluster Survey (MICS), with a total sample size of 14,278 children aged 6–12 years. Bivariate analysis, crude and adjusted log-binomial models were used to assess the relationships between dropout and risk factors. Overall, 1.68% of the children dropped out, with increased rates observed among males (ARR = 2.44, 95% CI: 1.63–3.64) and children aged 9–12 years at the beginning of the school year had a higher risk of dropout (ARR = 1.83, 95% CI: 1.15–2.93). Mymensingh presented the highest dropout rate, 3.82 (ARR = 3.82, 95% CI: 1.59–9.18) times higher than Barishal. Children who did not read books or were not read to at home had 14.47 (ARR = 14.47, 95% CI: 9.30–22.51) times higher risk of primary school dropout. To reduce primary school dropouts in Bangladesh, addressing gender inequalities, regional disparities, and inadequate home reading activity is essential. Strengthening early childhood education initiatives, promoting home-based literacy activities, supporting older children in their grades, and implementing targeted interventions in disadvantaged regions may help reduce primary school dropout in Bangladesh.
nc6616cee15fe: Understanding forest canopy dynamics is critical for assessing the condition, resilience, and conservation priorities of protected landscapes. This study evaluated the spatiotemporal and seasonal variation in mapped forest canopy density within the Orchha Wildlife Sanctuary, Madhya Pradesh, India, using multi-seasonal Sentinel-2 imagery and a Google Earth Engine (GEE)-based Random Forest (RF) classification framework. Sentinel-2 data for pre-monsoon (March–May) and post-monsoon (October–December) periods in 2016 and 2024 were analyzed independently. Canopy-density information was derived from NDVI, NDMI, elevation, slope, and GLCM texture features and classified into four classes: non-forest, open, moderate, and dense canopy. The same RF procedure was applied to all four season-year datasets using NDVI-informed canopy-density strata and balanced reference sampling. Overall accuracy ranged from 97.80% to 98.95%, with Kappa coefficients of 0.970–0.986. The results indicated clear seasonal and interannual redistribution of mapped canopy-density classes. During the pre-monsoon period, non-forest and open classes decreased by 39.62% and 7.15%, respectively, while moderate and dense classes increased by 231.64% and 240.43%. During the post-monsoon period, moderate canopy increased by 26.01%, whereas dense canopy decreased by 9.46%. Within the common comparison area of 4,533.54 ha, transition analysis revealed substantial class persistence and redistribution, particularly among adjacent canopy-density classes such as open-to-moderate and dense-to-moderate transitions. Spatial changes were distributed across riparian, interior, and peripheral zones. Because 2016 used Level-1C top-of-atmosphere data and 2024 used Level-2A surface-reflectance products, interannual differences should be interpreted as changes in mapped canopy-density classes rather than precise biophysical changes in canopy structure. The framework provides a replicable approach for seasonal forest monitoring and spatially targeted conservation planning.
n8540fd59b684: Bovine anaplasmosis, caused by the tick-borne rickettsial pathogen Anaplasma marginale, is a significant threat to livestock health and productivity. The major surface protein 1a (MSP1a) is a widely used molecular marker for characterizing strain diversity, due to its variable N-terminal tandem repeats. In this study, we analyzed and updated the nomenclature classification of 157 A. marginale MSP1a sequences submitted to NCBI between 2013 and 2023, following the research by Cabezas-Cruz in 2013. We identified and classified 189 unique tandem repeats, reported their tick-transmissibility, predicted their secondary structures and B-cell epitopes, and analyzed amino acid variability. Following this, we conducted a comparative analysis with previously published datasets, which revealed new tandem repeat types, new positions of serine within tandem repeats, and high variation among B-cell epitope variants. We have also classified the unique R1 tandem repeats of the new MSP1a sequences into different ecoregion clusters based on the principal component analysis of NDVI values. This updated classification system enhances the molecular understanding of A. marginale diversity and may contribute to future developments in strain typing, epidemiological investigations, and vaccine research.
n55ddff330ccb: Educational support for nurses is essential to promote oral health management education for patients with diabetes. However, few studies have focused on supporting nurses in this context. This study explored the effects of an audiovisual material designed to support nurses’ patient education on oral health management in diabetes care. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with eight certified diabetes nurse educators. Data were analyzed using content analysis. Four main themes emerged: (1) enhancement of nurses’ individual learning (8/8 participants), including improved knowledge of the connection between oral health and diabetes; (2) promotion of professional development and reflection (5/8); (3) provision of new insights into patient care (7/8), particularly regarding patient motivation strategies; and (4) identification of implementation considerations in diabetes outpatient settings. The findings suggest that the audiovisual material, designed to complement an existing evidence-based educational guide, was perceived as useful and may support nurses’ learning and educational practices related to oral health education for patients with diabetes.
n383f7b7b0bc2: Objective This scoping review examines how climate-related stressors and infectious-disease conditions, including pandemic-related workplace disruptions, interact to influence worker health, vulnerability, and occupational resilience. The review focuses on shared exposure pathways, vulnerable worker populations, methodological patterns, policy gaps, and strategies for strengthening worker safety under compound hazards. Rather than treating pandemics as isolated events, the review uses pandemic conditions as a lens to understand broader, recurring occupational risks and to inform strategies for building safer and more resilient workplaces under compound hazards. Methods Following PRISMA-ScR guidelines, a structured literature search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar for English-language peer-reviewed and formally structured evidence sources published primarily between January 2020 and April 2025, with one pre-2020 policy study retained for foundational context. Out of 612 records initially identified, 10 studies or sources met the inclusion criteria across healthcare, agriculture, construction, emergency response, and other high-exposure sectors after systematic screening and eligibility assessment. Data were charted and synthesized by occupational sector, geographic region, exposure type, worker vulnerability, and methodological approach. Results The evidence indicates that climate-related and infectious-disease stressors frequently converge, amplifying physical, environmental, and psychosocial pressures on workers. Disproportionate risks were observed among migrant workers, informal laborers, low-income populations, older adults, women, and seasonal or cross-border agricultural workers, particularly where access to healthcare, legal protections, or adaptive infrastructure was limited. Most studies relied on descriptive, qualitative, cross-sectional, conceptual, or review-based designs, with limited use of predictive modeling, geospatial analysis, longitudinal evidence, or integrated datasets. Policy responses were often fragmented, with climate adaptation and infection-control measures addressed separately despite overlapping benefits. Conclusions Climate-related and infectious-disease stressors interact to reinforce occupational health inequities and expose persistent gaps in worker protection. The findings highlight the need for integrated, multi-hazard occupational health strategies that align climate adaptation, infection prevention, and psychosocial support. Embedding data-driven early-warning systems, equitable protections for vulnerable workers, and cross-sector coordination into occupational policies may help strengthen workforce resilience during routine operations as well as future climate extremes and public health crises. However, the findings should be interpreted with caution because of the limited number of available studies combining climate-related and infectious-disease occupational risks, heterogeneous study designs, and the emerging nature of the evidence base. Furthermore, since this scoping review maps evidence rather than formally grading evidence strength or testing causal relationships, recommendations should be interpreted as evidence-informed directions for future occupational-health planning and research.
n827f2624f6bc: Software requirements are written in natural language, so they are inherently ambiguous. This ambiguity results in the misinterpretation of the requirements and leads to an incorrect implementation of the system that does not meet the user’s needs. So, it is important for all the stakeholders to comprehend the requirements. The requirement statements revolve around the requirement entities. Identifying requirement entities is essential to understand requirements, and they are used in identifying coreferent entities, creating glossaries, producing summaries of documents, feature extraction, requirements classification, and domain understanding. Manual entity extraction is a labour-intensive task. Recently, transformer-based models have played an important role in improving entity extraction results, but they require extensive pre-training of models for domain-specific tasks. To overcome these challenges, the proposed automated approach is used to extract entities from software requirements without the need for manual efforts and a large dataset for pre-training. In this study, two widely used parsing techniques, constituency parsing and dependency parsing, are applied to extract noun phrase-based entities. In addition, a hybrid approach comprising the combined extractions of both parsers is developed. The dataset comprises the software requirements from the healthcare domain and is manually annotated to establish a gold standard for evaluation. Experimental results indicate that the hybrid approach achieves the best overall extraction performance among the evaluated methods. While the constituency parser achieves the highest precision, it exhibits comparatively lower recall. In contrast, the hybrid approach achieves the highest recall and F1-score while maintaining precision comparable to that of the constituency parser. These results demonstrate that the hybrid method provides a more effective solution for automatically extracting entities from software requirements by leveraging syntactic structures of sentences rather than relying on domain-specific model training.
n9c81dfe40ae7: Accurate prediction of bored pile settlement is a core element in reliable foundation design. While machine learning (ML) models demonstrate superior predictive capabilities compared to traditional analytical methods, their black-box nature and tendency to generate non-physical trajectories significantly hinder their practical application in geotechnical engineering. This study proposes a new computational framework that ensures physical consistency by combining Weighted Ensemble learning with SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) interpretation capabilities. The integrated structure incorporates linear regression (LR), Random Forest (RF), XGBoost, and multilayer neural networks (MLP) to capture the complex interaction between piles and soil through a database of 563 field static load test records. A two-stage hybrid optimization strategy, using Random Search combined with a Genetic Algorithm (GA), was implemented to optimize the global weight set. The results showed that the GA-Ensemble model achieved excellent accuracy on the independent test set (R2 = 0.958, NRMSE = 5.27%, RMSE = 0.380, MAE = 0.2322), successfully neutralizing the ladder errors of the tree model to recreate a smooth, continuous, and mechanically compliant load-settlement (P-S) trajectory. Notably, by converting the SHAP value to a real physical scale (millimeters), the study clarified the algorithm’s inference logic. SHAP dependency analysis demonstrated that the model successfully captures the coupling characteristics of elastic compression and geometric nonlinearity by identifying the interaction between external force (P) and free length (Lf). Local diagnostic decompositions precisely extract failure mechanisms, successfully quantifying the “systemic penalty” caused by elastic shortening of structures and foundation puncture even in very stiff soil layers. In short, the proposed method has gone beyond the limits of a purely interpolation tool, establishing a transparent and geomechanically reliable expert system for predicting settlement.
nb726426ce383: Visual impairment (VI) is a severe and prevalent complication of type 2 diabetes (T2D), particularly in high-risk populations, underscoring the critical need for early predictive strategies. A retrospective cross-sectional study was conducted to develop and validate machine learning (ML) predictive models for VI among patients with T2D in Saudi Arabia. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study to employ WOA and BWO as feature selection techniques to identify the most informative predictors of VI among Saudi patients with T2D. Predictive models were subsequently developed and compared using both clinically recommended features and algorithmically selected features derived from WOA and BWO to determine the optimal feature set for predictive performance. Medical records of 1,000 T2D patients (555 VI [55.5%]; 445 non-VI [44.5%]) from King Abdulaziz University Hospital were analyzed. Models were developed using an 80/20 stratified train-test split, with 5-fold cross-validation performed on the training set for internal validation. Patients were divided into two groups: those with HbA1c ≥ 6.5% (full dataset) and a clinically relevant high-risk subgroup with HbA1c > 8% (reduced dataset), which incorporated 19 recommended demographic, lifestyle, and lipid profile features. Models utilizing the reduced dataset consistently achieved superior performance across all algorithms. Among them, the WOA-CatBoost model demonstrated the highest performance (Accuracy = 0.95, AUC = 0.96, 95% CI: 0.94–0.98) using only 9 features, outperforming both the BWO-Random Forest (BWO-RF) model (Accuracy = 0.92, AUC = 0.90, 95% CI: 0.87–0.93) with 10 features and the baseline Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) model (Accuracy = 0.91, AUC = 0.94, 95% CI: 0.91–0.97) with 13 features. Bonferroni-corrected paired t-tests based on five-fold cross-validation accuracies (α = 0.017) confirmed a significant performance advantage of WOA-CatBoost over BWO-RF (t = 10.17, p ting WOA-CatBoost as the overall best-performing model. Key predictors identified across all three best-performing models included Hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c), body mass index (BMI), age, occupation, triglycerides (TG), type of food, and smoking. These findings demonstrate that WOA-CatBoost provides a clinically actionable, parsimonious predictive tool for VI risk stratification in T2D patients within the Saudi Arabian healthcare context.
n1ba75a5d410a: Background Preeclampsia (PE) with severe features threatens maternal and neonatal health. This study examined maternal and health–service factors associated with severe features and compared maternal and neonatal outcomes in Thailand. Methods This case–control study enrolled 156 postpartum women with PE (52 with and 104 without severe features) and 111 nurse–midwives in antenatal care, labor, and postpartum units across four Thai tertiary hospitals. Data were collected using postpartum and nurse–midwife questionnaires, and a maternal–neonatal health record form. Group differences were assessed using independent t–test, chi–square or Fisher’s exact tests. Multivariable binary logistic regression examined factors associated with severe features, adjusting for antenatal care visits and gravidity. Results Women with severe features more often had a history of PE (32.7% vs. 13.5%, p = 0.006) and differed in BMI distribution (p = 0.007). Three maternal factors were independently associated with severe features: history of PE (aOR = 5.99, 95% CI 2.13–16.83), BMI (aOR = 0.92 per kg/m2, 95% CI 0.86–0.98), and moderate versus low PE knowledge (aOR = 0.13, 95% CI 0.04–0.50). No health–service variable, including nurse training, was independently associated with severe features after adjustment (all p > 0.05). The model explained 29.4% (Nagelkerke R2) of the variance in PE severity and correctly classified 75.8% of cases. Infant birth weight was lower among women with severe features (p < 0.05); delivery mode, hospital stay, birth asphyxia, and NICU admission did not differ significantly. Conclusion A history of PE was associated with higher odds, and moderate (versus low) PE knowledge and higher BMI with lower odds, of severe features. These findings support prioritizing screening for prior PE history and structured antenatal knowledge counseling, together with adequately powered, multilevel studies to clarify the role of health–service factors in PE severity.
n123d735ac5cd: by Jacob B. Willes, Emma Robinson, Joshua K. Sponbeck, Derek A. Swanson, Dallin C. Swanson, Austin G. Goodrich, Steven P. Allen, A. Wayne Johnson Purpose The abductor hallucis (ABDH) contributes to foot function and mobility, which can influence quality of life, making accurate assessment of muscle volume important. While magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is often considered to be the reference standard of medical imaging, ultrasound (US) provides a cost-effective, rapid and dynamic way of assessing muscle size and function. This study aimed to evaluate the criterion validity and intrarater reliability of US-derived ABDH muscle volume measurements compared with MRI when image analysis was performed by assessors with limited experience. Methods Us And MRI were employed to measure the right and left ABDH muscle volume involving 22 participants (females = 12; males = 10). Following exclusions, 37 feet were available for analysis, with 36 complete MRI-US observations. Muscle volume of the ABDH was calculated across the muscle belly every 0.5 cm both manually by utilizing a truncated cone (TC) formula and with a semi-automated tool in the OsiriX (OX) software. Intrarater reliability was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC), standard error of measurement (SEm), and minimal detectable change (MDC). Criterion validity was evaluated using Pearson correlations, Bland-Altman analyses, and two one-sided tests (TOST) with a determined ±10% equivalence margin. Results Side-specific intrarater reliability was high across methods (ICC(3,1) = 0.932–0.997), with SEm values of 0.251–0.709 cm³ and relative MDC values of 4.48%−12.95%. Very strong associations were observed among methods (r = 0.906–0.995). Bland-Altman limits-of-agreement half-widths were 6.52%−9.84% for MRI-MRI and 17.86%−27.35% for MRI-US comparisons. All three method comparisons met the ± 10% equivalence criterion. Conclusion US-derived ABDH volume measurements demonstrated high intrarater reliability and statistical equivalence to MRI within the ± 10% margin. Although MRI-US comparisons showed greater individual-level variability than MRI-MRI comparisons, US may provide a practical alternative for assessing ABDH muscle volume when MRI is impractical.
nd8afc7120bbd: Previous work demonstrated that ectodermal cells exhibit greater susceptibility to SARS-CoV-2 than endodermal and mesodermal cells, raising concerns about potential vulnerability of the developing nervous system. We hypothesized that neural stem cells (NSCs) derived from human ectoderm are susceptible to SARS-CoV-2. Using pseudotyped viral particles representing both wild-type and Omicron spike variants, we confirmed efficient transduction in NSCs, with Omicron variants preferentially utilizing endocytosis-mediated entry. Inhibition of endocytosis with filipin and OcTMAB significantly reduced viral entry across all spike variants. Low glycosylation levels on NSCs facilitated viral entry, and enzymatic removal of glycosylation increased their susceptibility. Ectodermal infection by SARS-CoV-2 raises serious concern for potential teratogenic effects on the nervous system, possibly causing latent or subclinical anomalies not immediately evident at birth. Therefore, future clinical studies and long-term surveillance of infants and children exposed in utero are necessary to investigate and identify potential neurodevelopmental deficits.
n50ca8381efdd: Basalt fiber, a natural and eco-friendly reinforcement, has demonstrated superior properties compared with conventional synthetic fibers. This study investigates the effect of ageing on the mechanical and vibrational properties of Basalt/Epoxy, Glass/Epoxy, and Basalt-Glass/Epoxy hybrid composites. Laminates were fabricated using vacuum bagging, ensuring uniform fiber-matrix volume fractions, and then exposed to ageing in seawater, tap water, and distilled water for a duration of 80 days. The moisture absorption pattern followed Fickian diffusion, with seawater exhibiting the highest diffusion coefficients owing to matrix breakdown and osmotic influences. Tensile tests demonstrated a decrease in failure stress and modulus for all materials after ageing, with Glass/Epoxy composites experiencing the most notable degradation despite absorbing less moisture, indicating a weakening of the fiber-matrix interfacial bond. The hybrid laminates exhibited moderate tensile and vibrational characteristics and maintained mechanical performance better in harsh environments. Free vibration tests showed that the natural frequency diminished as mass increased due to moisture absorption, while damping factors rose after ageing. Overall, the combination of basalt and glass fibers enhanced environmental resilience, indicating their suitability for structural applications under challenging conditions.
n4e9b434f9b80: Urgent climate action is needed to keep warming below 2°C and protect hundreds of millions from climate collapse. As part of a broader Registered Report series, this study examined whether a longitudinal intervention designed to strengthen psychological correlates of pro-environmental behaviour could motivate n = 31 university students in The Netherlands to take climate action. The intervention was delivered over six weeks through interactive lessons and activities informed by psychological theories and interventions. The goal was to increase pro-climate behaviours by targeting 12 psychological factors. Participants completed surveys assessing these correlates, as well as ecological momentary assessments of individual and collective pro-climate behaviours before and after the intervention, and after three months (14 days each). A control group was included (n = 27). Results showed that 4 of the 12 psychological correlates increased significantly: emotional engagement, collective efficacy, the bottom-up theory of change (the belief that change can start from grassroots action and spread systemically) and climate appraisal. Three (except appraisal) remained elevated at the three-month follow-up. Civic engagement, advocacy and activism increased after the intervention in the experimental group relative to control group. The increase in activist behaviour was predicted by the development of a bottom-up theory of change.
n4993b2be88a7: Understanding the taxonomic affinity of putative avialan teeth is essential to assessing the geographic range and richness of Late Cretaceous toothed birds. Isolated teeth attributed to Avialae are known from numerous North American Late Cretaceous microfossil assemblages. However, because only a select few of these tooth types are known from teeth preserved in jaws, their taxonomic affinities remain uncertain. Several key morphologies used to diagnose avialan teeth are also present in non-avialan theropods and crocodyliforms, leading some to question whether many such isolated teeth belong to birds. Here, we provide detailed descriptions and high-resolution images of avialan teeth from the Late Cretaceous Prince Creek Formation (PCF) of northern Alaska. A total of 105 isolated teeth were identified as avialan and can be divided into seven distinct morphotypes. Crucially, decades of extensive microfossil sampling have failed to produce any evidence of crocodyliforms in the PCF, allowing us to rule out this possible identity. Further, the teeth described here can be distinguished from those of all non-avialan theropods known in the PCF. Our morphotypes thus provide an important framework for identifying bird teeth in other Late Cretaceous microfossil assemblages as well as understanding avialan diversity before the K–Pg extinction.
n760d688f9262: Hybrid quantum–classical machine learning on noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices suffers from three coupled overheads: hardware miscalibration, classical syndrome-decoding latency and shot noise on gradient estimators. We present quantum calibration and observable processing (QCOP), a unified closed-loop control layer integrating a spectral calibration engine (SCE), a hierarchical syndrome decoder (HSD) and an observable compression layer (OCL) within a single GPU-accelerated pipeline. Three theoretical bounds characterize the joint effect on logical error rate (LER), convergence rate and observable variance. On device-calibrated noise-model simulators (n=20 seeds), QCOP achieves up to 2× wall-clock training speed-up and approximately 40% variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) energy error reduction relative to the unaugmented baseline. A hardware pilot on ibm_nairobi at surface-code distance d=5 (2000 syndrome volumes, 8192 shots each, single calibration window) yields a 1.6× latency reduction and 1.9× LER reduction for the HSD over minimum-weight perfect matching (MWPM)—directionally consistent with simulation but quantitatively smaller, indicating noise sources beyond the model. This pilot exercises the HSD alone: the SCE and the OCL have not been run on physical hardware, and the three modules have never been executed jointly on a device. The end-to-end QCOP benefits—speed-up, energy error reduction and variance reduction—are therefore not hardware-validated, and end-to-end hardware validation of all three modules remains future work. Code and model weights are available at https://github.com/hekimoghlu/QCOP.
nf33364b8015d: The synthesis of monolayer graphene has progressed from exfoliation to bottom-up strategies, enabling increasing atomic-level control. This review compares key routes, chemical vapour deposition (CVD), SiC epitaxy, arc discharge, molecular assembly and single-atom catalysts (SACs) and evaluates their mechanisms, scalability and quality bottlenecks. CVD remains the most mature and scalable approach, delivering centimetre-scale-single-crystal films through optimized substrates, roll-to-roll annealing and dry transfer, yet transfer-induced defects and wafer-scale non-uniformity persist. SiC epitaxy enables transfer-free, wafer-scale graphene with well-aligned domains, but requires high temperatures and costly wafers. Arc discharge offers catalyst-free production of crystalline graphene flakes, although monolayer yield and purity remain limited. Molecular assembly provides unmatched structural programmability and atomic precision in nanoribbons and nanographene islands, typically restricted to micrometre scales and stringent conditions. SAC-mediated growth represents a precision limit, where isolated metal atoms catalyse single-carbon insertion or removal at graphene edges, though current demonstrations remain largely single-event observations. Complementing these routes, artificial intelligence/machine learning is increasingly used for parameter optimization, predictive modelling of domain size/uniformity/defects and automated quality control (convolutional neural network/ generative modelling and YOLO-based defect detection). Overall, industrially viable, defect-free monolayer graphene will require combining scalable growth, transfer-free integration, atomic-precision and AI-enabled closed-loop optimization.
na1ff310586e8: Generative agents powered by large language models (LLMs) demonstrate human-like characteristics through sophisticated natural language interactions. Their ability to assume roles and personalities based on predefined character biographies has positioned them as cost-effective substitutes for human participants in social science research. This paper explores the validity of such persona-based agents1 in representing human populations; we recreate the HEXACO personality inventory experiment by surveying 310 GPT-4 powered agents, conducting factor analysis on their responses, and comparing these results to the original findings presented by Ashton et al. (Ashton et al. 2004 J. Pers. Soc. Psychol. 87, 707–721 (doi:10.1037/0022-3514.87.5.707). Our results found (i) a coherent and reliable personality structure was recoverable from the agents’ responses demonstrating partial alignment to the HEXACO framework, (ii) the derived personality dimensions were consistent and reliable within GPT-4, when coupled with a sufficiently curated population, and (iii) cross-model analysis revealed variability in personality profiling, suggesting model-specific biases and limitations. We discuss the practical considerations and challenges encountered during the experiment. This study contributes to the ongoing discourse on the potential benefits and limitations of using generative agents in social science research and provides useful guidance on designing consistent and representative agent personas to maximize coverage and representation of human personality traits, while highlighting potential limitations of applying human psychometric frameworks to generative agents.
neb1570ec24da: Loot boxes are randomized rewards in video games. Meta-analyses suggest relationships between loot box spending and problem gambling symptomatology, and early longitudinal evidence suggests loot box purchasers migrate into conventional gambling at higher rates than non-purchasers. Regulatory responses vary across jurisdictions, and even in jurisdictions that have banned loot boxes, evidence suggests their presence in games remains common. Consequently, consumers are often responsible for regulating their own, and their children’s, loot box purchasing. To effectively achieve this, consumers must first be able to identify loot boxes. Here, we investigated consumer accuracy in identifying critical features of loot boxes. Participants were tasked to identify basic facts about, pictures of, and receipts generated by loot boxes. Parents and non-gamers, compared with non-parents and gamers, respectively, were poorer at identifying loot boxes. Our results suggest that parents and non-gamers may be less equipped to make informed loot box purchasing decisions compared with non-parents/non-guardians and gamers, respectively. This may pose risks for parents and unaware incipient gamers. These are the first findings providing objective evidence about the relative ability of consumers to identify, and thus self-regulate purchases of, loot boxes and suggest that parents and non-gamers may require support to ensure informed purchasing decisions.
n05c6c4984c30: In human language, word order impacts how words are categorized and understood (as nouns, verbs etc.). We have demonstrated that this effect extends to non-linguistic stimuli, suggesting that the impact of sequence order on stimulus categorization is a domain-general, rather than language-specific cognitive process. Here, we ask if this process is evolutionarily conserved in other non-human primates. We developed a non-linguistic experiment and tested rhesus macaques (Macaca mulatta) and bonobos (Pan paniscus). Participants first learned to categorize shapes (as rounded, squared or pointed). We next assessed how they categorized ambiguous morph shapes by combining exemplars from each category. We provided sequential information by training the animals to select shapes in a specified order: rounded, then squared and then pointed. Finally, we assessed whether presentation in specific positions in this learned sequence would impact subsequent categorization of ambiguous morph shapes. In humans, an ambiguous morph was more likely to be categorized as the shape it replaced in a sequence. Non-human primates, however, showed no such effect, categorizing stimuli independent of their position in a sequence. This suggests that the tendency to infer category membership from sequence order is not shared across primates, and may have evolved more recently in the human lineage.
nbd05594d8f94: Mirror life presents a low-likelihood but high-severity global biosecurity threat that has attracted the attention of bioscientists, governments and international security organizations. However, current analytical techniques are not fit to identify mirror life biohazards. Herein, we propose the first assay method for screening against mirror life. This approach is based upon optical circularly polarized luminesce (CPL) signatures generated by fluorescent probes, which bind to subcellular targets (e.g. membranes, organelles, nucleic acids, etc.). Probes can either be achiral or be intrinsically chiral. We set out why a multi-probe reporter panel approach incorporating many CPL-generating probes is necessary to identify mirror life with a high degree of confidence (i.e. avoiding false positives). The distinct CPL signatures can be analysed via recent innovations in CPL detection, i.e. rapid CPL spectroscopy, CPL microscopy (enantioselective differential chiral contrast, EDCC, imaging) and CPL EDCC cameras. While these are advanced technologies, they share the same fundamental optical principles as three-dimensional cinema glasses and so are amenable to scaling and portable applications. The CPL assay approach to mirror life screening could be a useful tool for screening against mirror life biohazards and ensuring compliance with any potential future international legislation against mirror-life research.
ne6f5460adcac: We propose an iterative programmatic planning (IPP) framework that solves grid-based tasks by using large language models (LLMs) to synthesize interpretable, executable programs that act as agent policies mapping environment states to action sequences, rather than relying on traditional search or reinforcement learning. Alongside prompting strategies such as direct code generation, pseudocode conditioned refinement and curriculum-based prompting, IPP centres on an iterative refinement mechanism that updates code from coarse, task-level feedback. We evaluate our approach using six leading LLMs and two challenging grid-based benchmarks (grid-based reasoning for assessing spatial planning (GRASP) and MiniGrid). Our IPP framework demonstrates improvements over direct code generation for five of the six models, with net energy gains ranging from a few per cent to roughly threefold and, for Gemini-2.5-Pro, a sign flip from a negative baseline to a strongly positive score, establishes a new state-of-the-art result for GRASP and significantly outperforms direct elicitation from GPT-o3-mini (by 43% on the hardest MiniGrid task to 116% on GRASP). While code generation has a higher initial prompting cost compared to direct solution elicitation ($0.08 per task versus $0.002 per instance for GPT-o3-mini), the code can be reused for any number of instances, making the amortized cost significantly lower (by 400 times on GPT-o3-mini across the complete GRASP benchmark). Beyond performance gains, IPP produces reusable, human-readable policies that support transparent inspection and modification, underscoring the advantages of planning as program synthesis over per-instance inference. The code and results can be found at http://github.com/Mystic-Slice/LLM-Planning-CodeGen.
n3476bd0108c4: The Neogene fossil record of Patagonia provides important insights into the evolution and ecological diversification of marine predators in the Southern Hemisphere. Among these, Kawas benegasorum, an extinct seal from the Late Miocene Puerto Madryn Formation, represents the only record of a putative phocine (northern seals) in the Southern Hemisphere and preserves rare evidence of stomach contents. However, its original description was concise, and lacked detailed information on its dentition and stomach contents, leaving aspects of its morphology, phylogeny and paleoecology unresolved. We re-describe the holotype and only known specimen of K. benegasorum, providing the first comprehensive study of its postcranial morphology, new information on its dentition and a detailed examination of its stomach contents. We show that Kawas has both monachine- and phocine-like traits, with an overall morphology suggesting affinities with Monachinae. However, phylogenetic analyses yielded conflicting results, recovering Kawas either within Phocinae or in an unresolved position within Phocidae. The stomach contents indicate a piscivorous diet with coastal, benthic and demersal prey, broadly comparable to that of extant South American sea lions inhabiting the region. These results document early benthic nearshore foraging in pinnipeds and suggest dietary convergence across geological time in the western South Atlantic by the Late Miocene.
