n3489e2461cca: Several species rely on mechanisms to resolve conflicts and reduce their negative consequences, including reconciliation and third-party affiliation (i.e. post-conflict affiliative interactions between victims and aggressors, and between victims and third parties, respectively). Here, we studied reconciliation and third-party affiliation in two groups of wolves (n = 20) and three groups of wolves introgressed with dogs (i.e. second- or later-generation backcrosses of wolf-dog hybrids to wolves; n = 13), in captivity. We conducted behavioural observations of post-conflict affiliative interactions using continuous focal sampling for 2 minutes following an aggression, and during matched-control periods. Our results showed that both admixed and non-admixed wolves engaged in post-conflict affiliation consistent with reconciliation and third-party affiliation. Although we found no evidence that admixed wolves showed lower reconciliation or third-party affiliation than non-admixed wolves, social factors had different modulatory effects in admixed and non-admixed wolves. In particular, stronger social bonds promoted post-conflict affiliation in non-admixed wolves, whereas greater rank distance was associated with higher post-conflict affiliation in admixed wolves. Moreover, post-conflict affiliation was more likely following high-intensity aggression in both admixed and non-admixed wolves, and after unidirectional conflicts in the latter. These findings indicate that dog introgression may influence post-conflict behaviour in wolves and suggest that, while both admixed and non-admixed wolves engage in post-conflict affiliation, the mechanisms underlying them may partially differ.
n278be3486cb3: Pathogens exert strong selective pressure on group-living primates. In humans, disease defence includes both a biological and behavioural immune system, which includes the emotion of disgust and avoidance behaviours shaped by genetics, learning and culture. While pathogen avoidance is documented in nonhuman primates, little is known about how ecological and developmental factors influence pathogen sensitivity, that is, individual variation in pathogen avoidance. We conducted two studies to examine this in macaques. Our first study tested macaques (n = 54) from seven different species and four different rearing backgrounds in a visual food-choice task where food was either placed on a substrate with or without pathogenic cues. Macaques preferred feeding on non-contaminated substrates, with sanctuary-born individuals showing greater avoidance than former pets. Our second study tested sanctuary-born Japanese macaques (n = 55) from four groups; three groups had recently experienced an infectious disease outbreak. Macaques from exposed groups showed significantly higher avoidance of contaminated substrates. Together, our findings suggest that early life rearing experience and recent disease exposure shape pathogen sensitivity in macaques, demonstrating a flexible behavioural immune system in Old World monkeys. These findings suggest that flexible, context-sensitive pathogen avoidance is present in Old World monkeys, providing the behavioural foundations from which human disgust may have evolved.
nbb468375f3b7: This study examines eco-geomorphic changes on the exposed reef flat of Funafuti Atoll over the past 120 years to assess the relative influence of sea-level rise and storm events on reef flat and adjacent environments. Despite a documented sea-level rise of approximately 0.45 m during this period, we find no evidence of long-term structural or ecological alteration on the reef flat itself. We attribute this stability to emergent properties that may buffer against sea-level–driven impacts observed elsewhere. By contrast, significant geomorphic adjustments occurred at the reef flat margins: spur destruction on the seaward edge and increased island elevation landward. These changes reflect cyclone-induced disturbances combined with relative submergence of the reef flat. Notably, this research provides the first empirical evidence linking rising sea levels to increased atoll island elevation. Our findings suggest that future trajectories of reef flats and islands will depend on site-specific interactions among eco-geomorphic inheritance, sea-level rise rates and storm frequency. While these results are broadly applicable to emergent reef flats typical of Indo-Pacific atolls, further comparative studies across diverse reef flat types are essential to refine predictions of atoll resilience under accelerating climate change.
nd651be6e3ee7: Live trapping is central to behavioural ecology, yet whether post-capture behaviour reflects consistent among-individual differences and how it is modified by repeated captures remain poorly understood. Here, we repeatedly captured wild individuals of the rodent Apodemus mystacinus and temporarily held them in a standardised wooden experimental box. We then allowed them to voluntarily exit the box near the capture location and continuously recorded their behaviour for 5 minutes. Using multilevel, multivariate and continuous-time multi-state models, we characterise the sequence of behavioural states from confinement to escape. We also test whether capture experience reorganises individual behavioural trajectories and whether individual characteristics, such as body mass and sex, mediate behavioural transitions across capture–recapture events. We show that there is among-individual variation in the measured post-capture behaviours and that repeated captures reorganise the structure and sequential organisation of behavioural responses after individuals exit a trap. Importantly, we also show that recapture experience and body mass are associated with an increased tendency towards rapid escape. In contrast, we find that sex has no detectable effects. Our findings highlight that behaviours expressed immediately after trap release do not represent individuals' undisturbed ecological baseline, but instead experience-dependent responses shaped by individuals' cumulative history of interactions with their environment.
n48c96255a0d5: Visual memory is known to be influenced by objective image properties, including image size and contrast, as well as visual category. However, the influence of illusory perceptual experience on memory remains less understood. Here we investigated whether face pareidolia, a robust illusory phenomenon where certain stimuli elicit a face-like percept despite not being real faces, influences memory. While we assumed illusory faces would be remembered better than matched control images since they are surprising, interesting, draw more attention and may be associated with longer observation times, old-new recognition memory sensitivity was not consistently influenced by the face illusion. Surprisingly, decision criterion was more liberal for illusory faces than for other categories, and this effect scaled with illusory strength such that participants were more likely to report having seen illusory faces for stronger illusory face percepts. In a two-alternative-forced-choice recognition memory paradigm that minimizes criterion influence, we found that the tendency to report having seen illusory faces is present even for unseen images. Further analyses, involving confidence ratings indicated our findings probably reflect a heightened sense of familiarity for illusory faces and not genuine false memory. Our results suggest that during retrieval, illusory faces influence decisions independently of the actual memory trace.
n36a3e5b9a607: Over the past decade, psychology has embraced transparency and reproducibility reforms to address the replication crisis, raising the question of whether these signals help legal decision makers identify reliable psychological evidence. This study examines how these reforms influence perceived study reliability and downstream decision-making. We hypothesized that higher methodological quality (larger sample sizes, preregistration, and replications or meta-analyses) would increase perceived reliability and influence guilt judgements. We conducted an online vignette experiment, including individuals with doctorates and laypersons, who evaluated fictitious legal cases accompanied by research summaries varying in sample size (low versus high), preregistration status (preregistered versus not) and study design (primary study versus replication versus meta-analysis). Larger sample sizes consistently enhanced perceived reliability across both groups, whereas preregistration did not. Doctorate participants rated replications and meta-analyses as more reliable than primary studies; laypersons did not differentiate among designs. Importantly, none of the methodological quality cues influenced guilt judgements, despite shaping reliability judgements. This suggests that recognizing methodological quality alone may not shape downstream decisions. Future research should replicate the evidence in more ecologically valid legal designs (e.g. expert testimony) and with a broader range of methodological indicators to better understand how methodological quality influences perceived reliability and applied reasoning.
ne4872ca750bd: The quality control of commercial fuels is of paramount importance for ensuring regulatory compliance, engine performance and consumer protection. In Brazil, the composition of gasoline and anhydrous ethanol fuel blends is subject to specific regulatory requirements, and deviations from the prescribed proportions may compromise fuel quality and facilitate economically motivated adulteration. This study proposes a preliminary methodology for the identification of irregularities in binary gasoline and anhydrous ethanol fuel blends based on a Love-wave sensor. The proposed approach exploits the multiphysics response of the sensor to variations in the physicochemical properties of the liquid mixtures, which are directly influenced by their volumetric composition. The results demonstrate that changes in the proportions of the constituent liquids produce distinguishable variations in the sensor response, enabling the identification of different blend compositions. The proposed methodology therefore demonstrates the feasibility of employing Love-wave sensors as a rapid and potentially field-deployable screening tool for the preliminary assessment of irregular fuel blends in Brazil. Such an approach may contribute to more efficient fuel quality surveillance by reducing analysis time and operational costs while supporting subsequent confirmatory analyses using conventional laboratory techniques.
n4fe07412adb7: The dynamics of gene regulatory networks (GRNs) is governed by the interaction between deterministic biochemical reactions and molecular noise. To understand how GRNs process information during cell state transitions, we study stochastic dynamics derived from a Boolean network model via its representation on the parameter space of Gaussian distributions, equipped with the Fisher information metric. Restricting our analysis to transitions towards a single attractor, this reformulation reveals that dynamics along the gradient flows of the Kullback–Leibler (KL) divergence requires isotropic decay rates across all nodes, and that the noise intensity quantitatively determines the potential differentiation between the initial and final states. Furthermore, we show that the Fisher geodesics, previously identified with minimal biological cost, would require the suppression of noise and lead to deterministic dynamics that lacks biological relevance. This suggests that some departure from minimal cost is necessary for cell differentiation. Our approach frames noise and decay rates as fundamental control parameters, providing a geometric principle for the analysis and design of synthetic networks.
n7716545683e7: Lateral palatal foramina have been proposed as osteological correlates for baleen in fossil mysticetes. A recent study reported significantly elevated foramina counts in extant mysticetes relative to terrestrial artiodactyls (Ekdale et al. 2024 Sci. Rep. 14, 10174 (doi:10.1038/s41598-024-60673-8)). However, that analysis drew conclusions about fossil taxa despite not including any fossil taxa in its analysis. Here, we merge the datasets of Peredo et al. (Peredo et al. 2022 Sci. Rep. 12, 11448 (doi:10.1038/s41598-022-15684-8)) and Ekdale et al. (Ekdale et al. 2024 Sci. Rep. 14, 10174 (doi:10.1038/s41598-024-60673-8)) and add palatal foramina counts for eight stem mysticetes, producing a combined dataset of 195 specimens. Stem mysticetes are statistically indistinguishable from terrestrial artiodactyls in the number of palatal foramina (stem mysticete median = 4; artiodactyl median = 3) and significantly different from extant mysticetes (median = 46.5). Finer taxonomic analysis reveals that the elevated mysticete signal is driven by Balaenopteroidea. Balaenidae and Neobalaenidae, despite bearing baleen, do not exhibit elevated counts. Moreover, the elevated counts in Balaenopteroidea are a condition shared with Hippopotamidae, the closest living relatives of cetaceans. These results indicate that palatal foramina counts probably reflect the degree of soft tissue vascularization rather than the presence of baleen. Lateral palatal foramina counts cannot be used to infer baleen in fossil whales, and phylogenetic bracketing remains the most defensible framework for inferring baleen in fossil cetaceans.
n48818e4c42ce: Low body condition can promote risky foraging, but whether condition dependence differs across life stages remains unclear. Using field and laboratory studies, we tested whether residual body condition (RBC) predicted foraging under moonlight-mediated predation risk in the Amazonian sand knifefish, Gymnorhamphichthys rondoni. This species has a 2-year lifespan and a single late second-year breeding season. Because adults have less time than juveniles to recover condition before breeding, we predicted stronger condition dependence in adults. Among wild fish pooled across life stages, stomach fullness increased overnight on dark (lower-risk) but not bright moonlit (higher-risk) nights, when most stomachs were empty and non-empty stomachs occurred mainly in low-RBC fish. In experiments under laboratory-recreated moonlight, lower-RBC adults were active longer than higher-RBC adults on full-moon nights, as quantified by electric organ discharge rate. RBC did not predict adult activity on new-moon nights or juvenile activity on full- or new-moon nights. A full-moon interaction model showed a significantly stronger RBC–activity relationship in adults than in juveniles. In light-ramping trials, lower-RBC adults remained active at higher illuminance before hiding, whereas most juveniles did not hide. Our results are consistent with the asset-protection prediction of stronger condition-dependent risk-taking in adults facing late-life constraints than in juveniles.
n76321896bf23: The enantiornithes, a group of Mesozoic birds, have morphological features suggesting a precocial mode of development; however, their detailed physiological characteristics, particularly hatchling metabolic rates, have yet to be explored. Here, we retrodicted metabolic rates for four Lower Cretaceous enantiornithines: one hatchling, one adult from Las Hoyas, one early post-hatching juvenile and one post-juvenile individual from the Jehol Biota, using phylogenetic comparative analyses and a comprehensive dataset of extant birds spanning the altricial–precocial spectrum. By examining vascular density (related to resting metabolic rate (RMR)) and nutrient foraminal size (proportional to blood flow rate) as proxies, we inferred the metabolic scope of the hatchling enantiornithine and determined that it fell toward the precocial end of the altricial–precocial spectrum. The RMR values of the two enantiornithine chicks were retrodicted as 0.67 mlO2 h–1 g–0.93. The peak metabolic rate (PMR) retrodicted is twice the resting metabolism for the Las Hoyas hatchling. These results are consistent with a semi-precocial/precocial development characterized by independent locomotion by climbing using the wing claws soon after hatching. However, flapping flight may have been delayed, owing to incomplete ossification of the sternum, as observed in one hatchling specimen.
nbf2dea205261: Morphological modularity is known to favour evolutionary diversification by enabling different body regions to vary in response to functional and ecological demands. Despite their remarkable diversity in limb morphology and ecology, amphibians—and salamanders in particular—remain significantly under-represented in empirical tests of modularity. Using geometric morphometrics and phylogenetic comparative methods, we investigate patterns of shape variation, integration and modularity in the salamander autopodium. We first validated a landmark-based method to outline foot shape, demonstrating that image orientation does not affect shape analyses and that species can be reliably distinguished. We then applied this approach to a larger comparative dataset encompassing 149 salamander taxa across major lineages and ecological strategies. Our findings demonstrate that the salamander autopodium is functionally modular: the distal region (digits and interdigital region) shows more evolutionary lability than the proximal pes, while remaining integrated within a coordinated evolutionary system. Furthermore, the combinations of allometric, ecological and life-history factors account for a small but significant percentage of shape variation, with a low evolutionary signal in foot shape. Our results suggest that modular organization of the salamander foot may allow for morphological variation while still being limited by a common evolutionary and developmental history. By focusing on an understudied group and morphological system, this study provides new insight on how modularity influences limb evolution in tetrapods.
nc984f41ebcc8: When listening to novel music, extra-musical information about the musician may influence a listener's evaluations of the music. Here, we studied the extent to which information about the musicians’ Humanness, Morality and Sex, conveyed by their vocal timbre and tessitura, affected listeners’ emotional and aesthetic responses to their music. This online, pre-registered experiment followed a 2 (Humanness: Human vs. AI model) × 2 (Vocalist Sex: Male vs. Female) × 3 (Morality: Moral, Immoral, Neutral) mixed factorial design. Participants (n = 400) were randomly assigned to one of four groups, differing in Humanness and Vocalist Sex. Participants read three descriptions depicting a Moral, Immoral and Neutral behaviour and listened to three unfamiliar songs pseudorandomly paired with a description. Emotional and aesthetic responses to each song were measured using validated measures (GEMS-9 scale) and additional items assessing feelings of being Moved, Connected, perceived Beauty, Liking and perceived Creativity. As predicted, linear mixed-effects models revealed significant main effects of Morality for all dependent variables, with Immoral descriptions consistently yielding more negative ratings. Contrary to predictions, we observed no differences in responses to songs based on Humanness, no significant interaction between Morality and Humanness and no effect of Vocalist Sex on responses.
n96c4b330894d: Conceptualizations of recovery in gaming disorder (GD) remain relatively underdeveloped. While remission without formal treatment appears common in longitudinal data, the mechanisms through which it occurs have received little systematic attention. In contrast, natural recovery—the resolution of addictive problems without formal treatment—is well documented in substance and gambling research, where it has prompted broader reconceptualizations of how and where recovery unfolds. Using longitudinal qualitative data from Finland, Slovakia and South Korea, this case series examines how individuals who had previously experienced self-identified gaming-related problems reached recovery without successful intervention explicitly targeting their gaming behaviour. Six recurring recovery pathways were identified: axiological shift, social enforcement, gradual regulation, reflexive transformation, healing comorbidity and environmental transformation. Rather than centring on abstinence or direct symptom elimination, recovery emerged through reconfigurations of life structure, social roles and personal value hierarchies. In most cases, gaming did not disappear but was repositioned within a broader ecology of responsibilities and relationships. These findings suggest that natural recovery in GD may be better understood as a contextual and relational reconfiguration rather than solely as symptom reduction. The pathways identified here provide a conceptual stepping stone towards more comprehensive frameworks for understanding the recovery process in GD.
n8aaab5243703: Palladium–iron (Pd–Fe) bimetallic catalysis represents a pivotal strategy for advancing the sustainability of organometallic transformations. Herein, we report a facile and efficient synthetic protocol for Pd–Fe magnetic nanomaterials mediated by carbonyl iron, which proceeds without external reducing agents, surfactants or protective gases. In this approach, carbonyl iron serves a dual role as both the iron source and the reducing agent, while in situ generated carbon monoxide provides three essential functions: atmospheric protection, pressure regulation and crystal nucleus stabilization. This unique reaction system facilitates the co-deposition of zero-valent palladium (Pd0) and iron oxide (Fe2O3) onto pristine Fe3O4 surfaces, yielding magnetically recyclable Pd–Fe@Fe3O4 nanocomposites. Comprehensive characterization via high-resolution transmission electron microscopy, scanning electron microscopy, energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy mapping and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy confirms the well-defined hierarchical structure, uniform elemental distribution and controlled valence states of the as-synthesized materials. The resulting nanomaterials display a narrow particle size distribution (2–3 nm), high metal loading efficiency and low lattice mismatch. Preliminary catalytic evaluations reveal excellent activity of Pd–Fe@Fe3O4 in Suzuki–Miyaura cross-coupling reactions. Notably, similar performance is achieved with catalysts derived from other metal carbonyl precursors, underscoring the generality of this synthetic platform for designing efficient and recyclable bimetallic nanocatalysts.
n0f07f315c00d: Backlash against the artificial intelligence (AI) industry is growing globally in recognition of the high costs and highly uncertain risks borne by society. General-purpose AI systems are sold predominantly on the basis of economic benefits, with little attention given to social or non-financial benefits. Policymakers tasked with regulating AI while balancing European Union (EU) rights and values with innovation and free market competition face a seemingly impossible task. A change of priorities is urgently needed in EU tech policy. Current policy predominantly focuses on risk mitigation rather than delivering socially beneficial technologies. EU tech policy should be rebalanced in favour of societal interests owing to the substantial (in)direct subsidies paid to support the AI industry via tax breaks, public funding, privileged access to public lands, resources, data and infrastructure and widespread deregulation. We propose adding a third goal to rebalance EU AI policy-making: happiness. When policymakers are deciding whether subsidies should be granted for the AI industry, they should require companies to concretely predict measurable benefits for happiness, and hold them accountable for delivering on their predictions. To unpack this proposal, we examine decades of research in psychology to identify key determinants of happiness, focusing on three widely accepted traits: relatedness, competence and autonomy.
nb727a4d0902b: Sustainably closing agricultural yield gaps remains a central challenge for advancing global food security while conserving biodiversity. This article develops a theoretical perspective on why sustainable intensification (SI) is limited in many lower-income countries, despite the technological feasibility of improving yields in these places. It explores these constraints to SI through two case studies of expanding commodity frontiers: (i) beef in the Brazilian Amazon and Cerrado and (ii) cocoa in West Africa. We find similar barriers to SI across the cases, including limited tenurial, financial, knowledge and cultural support, community-level risks to investment and cheap land favouring agricultural expansion. At the same time, both cases reveal potential for rapid intensification, as demonstrated by success in selected locations. The analysis helps explain why many promising SI strategies have achieved limited uptake in countries where land for expansion is still relatively abundant. The article also identifies a more optimistic pathway: ambitious economic and institutional reforms, well-funded community-level technical and financial investments, and smart conservation policies could unlock joint gains for food security and biodiversity. Global policy and finance changes have opened windows for this coordinated policy agenda, but improved demand-side policies are also needed to tip low-yielding agricultural systems onto new trajectories.
n4eb2c71de716: A well-established inverted U-shape relationship links stimulus complexity and human music preference, with preferences peaking at intermediate levels. We investigated whether preference for intermediate complexity is unique to humans or shared with other species. We compared the acoustic preferences of humans and budgerigars, a species known for their vocal learning and pattern recognition abilities, using a three-option place preference paradigm. Participants were presented with choices between stimuli of different, computationally defined complexity: pitch sequences with tones arranged either randomly (high complexity), repeating patterns with changes (medium) or fully repetitive patterns (low). Our results demonstrate that, without specific goals or external rewards, both humans and budgerigars spontaneously exhibit a nonlinear (intermediate) preference profile, indicating a pattern consistent with an inverted U-shape relationship. Because a U-shape relationship may reflect a strategy to seek informative sources maximally useful for learning—that is, for building and refining internal models of the environment—this preference in the acoustic domain may support vocal learning. However, further testing could determine whether it also exists in vocal non-learning species. Because vertebrates show inverted U-shape responses in a variety of non-auditory contexts, our findings may stem from general processes, but potentially depend on vocal learning to translate to acoustic contexts.
nbd8ce6ce9af5: A simple strategy was developed to fabricate self-supporting bioanodes from graphitized palm-tree-branch powder for application in membrane-less microbial fuel cells (MFCs). Palm tree branches were graphitized at 900°C, 1000°C and 1100°C, ground into fine powder, blended with bitumen and starch, compression-moulded and thermally treated to produce robust anodes. The resulting electrodes were evaluated in an air-cathode, single-chamber MFC using raw sewage wastewater without external microbial inoculation or nutrient addition. Structural and electrochemical analyses showed that the prepared anodes possessed rough porous surfaces, stable carbon-dominated electrochemical behaviour and improved conductivity compared with an activated-carbon-based anode. Among the investigated samples, the anode prepared from palm branches graphitized at 1000°C exhibited the best overall performance. In sewage containing 5g l−1 sodium acetate, this anode delivered a maximum power density of about 1300 mW m−2, which was nearly 25 times higher than that of the activated-carbon-based anode (approx. 52 mW m−2). Even under electrolyte-free conditions, the same anode generated a maximum power density of about 400 mW m−2, indicating that intrinsically retained inorganic species, particularly KCl, may contribute to sustaining MFC operation without external electrolyte addition. In contrast, NaCl showed a much weaker promoting effect than sodium acetate. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy confirmed relatively low ohmic and charge-transfer resistances under the optimum condition.
n49ed5391517a: Earthworms (Lumbricidae) are moisture-loving soil-dwellers that can be categorized into two feeding guilds with distinct behaviours: detritivores and geophages. Detritivores feed on litter fragments and geophages on smaller litter particles mixed with soil. When earthworms move within and across soil layers to forage, soil characteristics might influence the scale of these movements and their detectability to predators. To investigate the extent to which the detection of earthworm movements and the vibrations they thereby generate is affected by soil moisture, we used an innovative method to detect and quantify vibrations of moving earthworms emitted through the soil. We designed a mesocosm experiment in which we recorded, with a geophone, the movement-induced vibrations of detritivores and geophages in drier and wetter soils. Earthworm vibrations were detected best at 200 Hz and were detected significantly more in wetter than in drier soils. Moreover, in wetter soils, vibrations induced by detritivores were detected more frequently and at higher intensities than those of geophages. These findings suggest differences in activity levels between detritivores and geophages, as a function of soil moisture content. The observed activity patterns are likely to have food web consequences because earthworm consumers relying on mechanoreceptors to detect prey might detect detritivores more often, specifically in wetter soils.
n690d6e630b73: A newly synthesized azo ligand, 1-((5-allyl-2-hydroxy-3-methoxyphenyl)diazenyl)anthracene-9,10-dione (H-MND), derived from an anthraquinone nucleus coupled with the natural phenol (eugenol), was employed to prepare Co(II), Ni(II), Cu(II), Rh(III) and Pd(II) complexes, with the ligand proposed to adopt a tridentate coordination mode. Anthraquinone derivatives and natural phenols are recognized for diverse pharmacological activities, making them valuable scaffolds for the design of bioactive ligands. The synthesized compounds were characterized by FT-IR, UV–vis, NMR spectroscopy, mass spectrometry, elemental analysis, thermal analysis thermogravimetric-differential scanning calorimetry (TGA-DSC), assessment of chlorine content, magnetic susceptibility and molar conductance measurements, which collectively suggested predominantly non-electrolytic behaviour. In the 1,1-diphenyl-2-picrylhydrazyl (DPPH) assay, the Ni(II) complex exhibited the highest antioxidant activity among the synthesized compounds, with an IC50 value significantly different from that of gallic acid (t = 4.31, p ˂ 0.01). Only the Pd(II) complex displayed activity towards plasmid DNA consistent with partial cleavage in the absence of externally added redox agents. Furthermore, activity mimicking phenoxazinone synthase was evaluated for the Cu(II) and Co(II) complexes, revealing system-specific catalytic behaviour. These results support further investigation into the biomedical and catalytic potential of these metal complexes.
n970d7df595d5: Coral reefs deliver vital services via a complex three-dimensional framework sustained by the balance between calcium carbonate production and erosion, or the net carbonate budget state. In many tropical western Atlantic reefs, ecological decline has reduced carbonate production, yielding near-neutral or negative budgets. Yet some reefs retain high coral cover and, theoretically, should also have high net positive budgets, yet often show modest carbonate accumulation. We used the remote reef of Cayo Arenas in the Campeche Bank, Gulf of Mexico, to test whether in reefs under suboptimal (variable) environmental conditions, high coral production is offset by robust bioeroder communities, producing neutral budgets. At 14 sites, we quantified carbonate producers and bioeroders to estimate gross production, bioerosion and net budget states. Despite relatively high live coral cover, mean net carbonate budgets did not differ significantly from a neutral (zero) state, despite a positive net budget (0.7 ± 0.5 SE kg CaCO3 m−2 yr−1) and substantial site-to-site variability (range: −2.3 to 4.3 kg CaCO3 m−2 yr−1). Crucially, this neutrality arose not from depressed biological activity (as in degraded reefs) but from an active equilibrium: elevated carbonate production coupled with substantial bioerosion. These reefs, therefore, represent a contemporary, functional reef state in net stasis. Distinguishing active-neutral reefs, where both production and bioerosion are elevated, from impoverishment-neutral reefs, where both are suppressed, is critical for predicting reef trajectories under environmental change and for targeting management, although near-stasis emerging from high carbonate turnover can appear functionally intact yet operate with limited buffering capacity against net carbonate loss.
ne8920f9bfb49: Cultural traditions shape how animals approach ecological problems. Over the last two decades, Ugandan chimpanzees (Pan troglodytes schweinfurthii) have engaged with the honey-trap experiment, an apparatus mimicking a beehive, while relying on their cultural knowledge. Here, we compared the behaviour of three Ugandan chimpanzee communities in the experiment, adding a previously untested community, the Mwera South chimpanzees of Bugoma Forest. First, we tested whether communities varied in their engagement with the experiment and investigated whether differences lay in individual or community-based characteristics. Second, we analysed individual variation within the same culture, particularly focusing on the new data coming from Bugoma Forest. We found that only the Kanyawara chimpanzees of Kibale Forest displayed a dedicated instrumental method, stick use, realized in their cultural knowledge and expressed by most members of the community, congruent with the largest engagement with the resource and suggestive of a general positive cultural attitude towards honey. By contrast, the two other communities appeared to lack a cultural attitude towards honey, with no attached tool technique overall. Nevertheless, there were also large inter-individual differences. Notably, Bugoma chimpanzees displayed undescribed behavioural flexibility, using a range of tool behaviours, including both stick and leaf tool use, a pattern never documented before. Cultural attitudes toward resources thus constitute an additional layer to culture in addition to instrumental knowledge and coexist with individual motivational traits in influencing the realization of cultural behaviour.
nd1b971a966db: By the mid-twentieth century, the previously booming bird feather trade was a fraction of what it was in its prime, allowing for the recovery of many bird species. We use a qualitative impact evaluation method to assign probable causality to different drivers of this change, ultimately providing expert-supported explanations of how a large-scale behaviour change was enacted to benefit conservation. We outline a method for applying general elimination methodology plus (GEM+), accounting for different facets of evidence reliability, to generate conclusions on most strongly supported causes of change. GEM+ addresses calls for an increase in impact evaluation in conservation, which will require a range of tools, including qualitative, to fill. Analysis of diverse evidence using GEM+ suggests that conservation advocacy, interacting with broader contextual factors, plausibly contributed to a shift in public behaviour that was instrumental in the passage of the Plumage Act and the subsequent end of the trade. This case study has widespread implications for designing effective behaviour change campaigns, as well as providing a framework for conducting impact evaluations in a range of conservation settings.
n5cc5b50de041: Planning is critical for adaptive behaviour in a changing world, because it lets us anticipate the future and adjust our actions accordingly. While prefrontal cortex is crucial for this process, it remains unknown how planning is implemented in neural circuits. Prefrontal representations were recently discovered in simpler sequence memory tasks, where different populations of neurons represent different future time points. We demonstrate that combining such representations with the ubiquitous principle of neural attractor dynamics allows circuits to solve much richer problems, including planning. This is achieved by embedding the environment structure directly in synaptic connections to implement an attractor network that infers desirable futures. The resulting ‘spacetime attractor’ excels at planning in challenging tasks known to depend on the prefrontal cortex. Recurrent neural networks trained by gradient descent on such tasks learn a solution that precisely recapitulates the spacetime attractor – in representation, in dynamics, and in connectivity. Analyses of networks trained across different environment structures reveal a generalisation mechanism that rapidly reconfigures the world model used for planning, without the need for synaptic plasticity. The spacetime attractor is a testable mechanistic theory of planning. If true, it would provide a path towards detailed mechanistic understanding of how prefrontal cortex structures adaptive behaviour.
n92841ace8bd1: Adaptive behavior requires assigning emotional value to sensory cues and generalizing to similar stimuli. The prelimbic cortex (PL) is critical for threat expression and discrimination, yet its neuronal ensembles undergo substantial turnover over time. How stable population codes emerge despite this reorganization remains unknown. Using longitudinal calcium imaging in freely moving mice, we tracked PL activity for 30 days during auditory discriminative fear learning and retrieval. Despite substantial ensemble turnover, stable graded representations persisted in PL populations. A generalized linear model showed that the tone threat value explained graded activity better than freezing, indicating that PL primarily encodes stimulus significance. Population similarity across stimulus presentations was highest for shock-associated and highly generalized tones, suggesting a stable population code underlying threat generalization. Stable neurons preserved graded gradients across sessions, whereas learning modulated the rate of dynamic frequency-selective neurons. Together, these populations enabled stable threat-value coding despite ongoing ensemble reorganization.
nfd8d863c3b3b: Endosymbiotic bacteria can affect many ecological attributes of their insect hosts, including (in herbivorous insects) how they interact with plants where they feed. This raises the issue of whether deliberate endosymbiont introductions could be used to decrease crop damage caused by insect pests. Here, we investigate how transinfecting Rickettsiella viridis and Regiella insecticola endosymbionts into a novel pest aphid host, the Russian wheat aphid (Diuraphis noxia), influences population growth, alate production, dispersal ability, and crop damage. Both the Rickettsiella (originating from pea aphids) and Regiella (from green peach aphids) were stably maintained in their new host where they had contrasting effects. Rickettsiella increased the severity of aphid feeding damage on wheat and barley, resulting in greater leaf loss, chlorotic streaking, and higher aphid populations, whereas Regiella reduced aphid population growth and the severity of feeding damage by aphids. Their effects on dispersal morphology also differed: Regiella had no detectable impact on alate incidence, while Rickettsiella consistently suppressed wing formation in small cages, and in larger mesocosms with multiple wheat plants this endosymbiont suppressed dispersal. Endosymbiont-mediated changes in feeding damage did not involve the main plant immune response pathways: transinfected and wild type aphids induced similar levels of jasmonic acid, jasmonic acid-isoleucine, and salicylic acid in plant tissues, even though these plant defenses were strongly activated during aphid feeding. Novel endosymbionts can therefore modulate the severity of plant feeding damage by aphids as well as influencing aphid dispersal. Potential applications in controlling pest D. noxia populations are discussed.
n6d7777304da1: Ongoing experience is continuously processed in the context of past events. Divergence between current experience and memory-based predictions (i.e., a mnemonic prediction error; MPE) is theorized to be a signal that encoding, as opposed to retrieval, should be prioritized. We asked how MPEs place demands on control and attention-related processes, and whether these demands differ as a function of prediction strength. We investigated these questions across two experiments, wherein we recorded scalp electroencephalography and/or pupillometry as 101 young human adults performed an associative memory task. Strong MPEs, more so than weak MPEs, increased physiological indices of cognitive control (frontal theta), attention (posterior alpha and pupil size), and arousal (pupil size). Greater cognitive control (frontal theta) during strong MPEs promoted better learning of prediction-violating (i.e., unexpected) stimuli. Collectively, these findings reveal multiple pathways through which the mind and brain respond adaptively to violations of strong mnemonic predictions.
nd092406caa9d: Sumoylation is a post-translational modification that can regulate different physiological functions. Increased sumoylation, specifically conjugation of SUMO2/3 (small ubiquitin-like modifier 2/3), is detrimental to vascular health. However, the molecular mechanism mediating this effect is poorly understood. We used cell-based assays and mass spectrometry to show that p66Shc is a direct target of SUMO2 and that SUMO2 regulates p66Shc function via lysine-81 modification. To determine the effects of SUMO2-p66ShcK81 on vascular function, we generated Shc1K81R mice and crossbred them toLdlr-/- mice to induce hyperlipidemia. Next, to determine p66ShcK81-SUMO2ylation-induced changes in endothelial cell signaling, we performed mass spectrometry followed by Ingenuity Pathway Analysis. Our data reveal that p66Shc mediates the effects of SUMO2 on endothelial cells. Mass spectrometry identified that SUMO2 modified lysine-81 in the unique collagen homology-2 domain of p66Shc. SUMO2ylation of p66Shc increased phosphorylation at serine-36, causing it to translocate to the mitochondria, a step critical for the oxidative function of p66Shc. Notably, sumoylation-deficient p66Shc (p66ShcK81R) was resistant to SUMO2-induced p66ShcS36 phosphorylation and mitochondrial translocation. Shc1K81R mice were resistant to endothelial dysfunction induced by SUMO2ylation and hyperlipidemia. Ingenuity Pathway Analysis revealed multiple signaling pathways regulated by p66ShcK81-SUMO2ylation in endothelial cells, highlighting JAK-STAT as a major pathway affected by SUMO2-p66ShcK81. Collectively, our work reveals SUMO2-p66Shc signaling as a fundamental regulator of vascular endothelial function. We discovered that p66ShcK81 is an upstream modification regulating p66Shc signaling and mediates hyperlipidemia-induced endothelial dysfunction and oxidative stress.
nd29d584f049f: Prison work has become a focus of research in corrections, with studies examining deleterious effects of nearly every aspect of the occupation. Correction officers navigate a variety of organizational and operational stressors within a complex occupational culture. This article identifies potentially harmful aspects of the occupation and reviews empirical findings related to officer well-being, incorporating direct accounts from correction officers. The review highlights prominent stressors that increase risk for adverse behavioral, emotional, and physical and mental health outcomes among officers, including the unique contribution that violence and trauma exposures have on officer mental health and suicide. Developing and offering evidence-based well-being initiatives and leveraging officers’ social support networks are potentially promising mechanisms by which to limit the negative impacts of correctional work. Although a long-term effort, addressing harmful aspects of the occupational culture will benefit correction officers, the incarcerated population, and correctional organizations.
nccfc88e18b60: Genetic evidence implicates immune dysfunction in Alzheimer’s disease (AD), yet the neuroimmune mechanisms operating in human tissue remain poorly defined. Here, we establish a modular human forebrain organoid platform that systematically integrates human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived microglia and CD8+ T cells to reconstitute multicellular AD pathology. This system enables functional interrogation of both innate and adaptive immune components in a human-relevant context. Using this platform, we demonstrate that microglia mediate amyloid-β clearance and neuronal maturation but also drive inflammatory activation and recruit CD8+ T cells through CCL4/5 signaling via CCR1/5 and CXCR3, establishing a neuroinflammatory feedback loop. Pharmacological targeting of CCR5 or CXCR3 blocks T cell recruitment and modulates autophagy in a microglia-dependent manner. This modular organoid platform provides a versatile tool for dissecting neuron–immune interactions and enables cell-type-specific therapeutic screening in human neuroinflammatory disease models.
n1258831cbbed: A critical phase of mammalian brain development takes place after birth. Neurons of the mouse neocortex undergo dramatic changes in their morphology, physiology, and synaptic connections during the first postnatal month, while properties of immature neurons, such as the capacity for robust axon outgrowth, are lost. The genetic and epigenetic programs controlling prenatal development are well studied, but our understanding of the transcriptional mechanisms that regulate postnatal neuronal maturation is comparatively lacking. By integrating chromatin accessibility and gene expression data from two subtypes of neocortical pyramidal neurons in the neonatal and maturing brain, we predicted a role for the Krüppel-like factor (KLF) family of transcription factors in the developmental regulation of neonatally expressed genes. Using a multiplexed CRISPR interference (CRISPRi) knockdown strategy, we found that a shift in expression from KLF activators (Klf6, Klf7) to repressors (Klf9, Klf13) during early postnatal development functions as a transcriptional ‘switch’ to first activate, then repress a set of shared targets with cytoskeletal functions including Tubb2b and Dpysl3. We demonstrate that this switch is buffered by redundancy between KLF paralogs, which our multiplexed CRISPRi strategy is equipped to overcome and study. Our results indicate that competition between activators and repressors within the KLF family regulates a conserved component of the postnatal maturation program that may underlie the loss of intrinsic axon growth in maturing neurons. This could facilitate the transition from axon growth to synaptic refinement required to stabilize mature circuits.
n0e217fe9b004: Innate T cells, including invariant natural killer T (iNKT) cells, mucosal-associated invariant T (MAIT) cells, and γδ T cells, bridge innate and adaptive immunity through rapid responses to nonpeptide antigens, metabolites, and stress-associated signals. In cancer, these populations can promote tumor surveillance through cytotoxicity, type 1 cytokine production, tissue-resident immune monitoring, and activation of broader antitumor networks. However, their functions are highly context dependent. Within suppressive tumor microenvironments, tumor-infiltrating unconventional T cell compartments may contain developmentally programmed innate-like subsets together with recruited or locally differentiated cells displaying dysfunctional, regulatory, or IL-17-associated features that support myeloid cell recruitment, chronic inflammation, immune evasion, and therapy resistance. This review discusses the major recognition pathways, functional states, microbiota- and metabolite-dependent regulation, and therapeutic targeting of iNKT, MAIT, and γδ T cells in cancer. We further highlight emerging strategies to harness these cells through endogenous activation, combination immunotherapy, and engineered cell platforms while limiting tumor-promoting inflammatory programs and treatment-associated toxicity.

nc7a4bda7d381: Caspases are cysteine-aspartic proteases that mediate both lethal and non-lethal cellular outcomes, including the promotion of tissue growth. However, the mechanisms underlying the differential regulation of these activities remain unclear. We have previously shown that among the two Drosophila executioner caspases, Dcp-1 and Drice, Dcp-1 promotes tissue growth in a non-lethal manner, independent of canonical apoptotic signaling. Herein, we demonstrated that overexpressed Dcp-1, but not Drice, was activated without canonical apoptosome components. TurboID-based proximity labeling revealed distinct proximal proteomes, among which Sirtuin 1, an Atg8a deacetylase, which promotes autophagy, was specifically required for Dcp-1 activation. Autophagy-related genes, including Bcl-2 family members Debcl and Buffy, are required for Dcp-1 activation. Structure-based prediction using AlphaFold3 further identified Bruce, an autophagy-regulated inhibitor of apoptosis, as a Dcp-1-specific regulator acting outside the apoptosome-mediated pathway. Physiologically, Bruce suppresses wing tissue growth. These findings indicate that non-lethal Dcp-1 activity is governed by the autophagy–Bruce axis, enabling distinct non-lethal functions independent of cell death.
nc46288cc936d: Mutations in Syntaxin11 (STX11), a Q-SNARE, result in a fatal immune disorder known as familial hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis 4 (FHLH4) in human patients. A key diagnostic feature of FHLH4 is defective T and natural killer cell cytotoxicity. Here, we show that STX11 directly binds and regulates Orai1, the pore-forming subunit of calcium release-activated calcium (CRAC) channels. CRAC channels enable store-operated calcium entry (SOCE) from the extracellular space and are crucial for granule exocytosis and nuclear factor of activated T cells (NFAT)-dependent gene expression in activated lymphocytes. STX11 depletion strongly inhibited SOCE, CRAC currents, NFAT activation, interleukin-2 gene expression, and degranulation in FHLH4 patient T lymphocytes and cell lines without affecting membrane trafficking. Remarkably, defects of cytolytic granule exocytosis, as well as interleukin-2 expression, could be reversed by ionomycin in patient T lymphocytes, and a constitutively active, H134S, mutant of Orai1 rescued calcium entry in STX11-depleted cells. Further analyses showed that STX11 ‘primes’ Orai1 for optimal on-site multimeric assembly, which was Stim independent but required for gating. Priming of ion channel pore subunits is, therefore, a primary function of specific SNAREs which may have preceded their role in membrane trafficking and vesicle fusion.
nf40a30d8b8f9: The last 110 years have seen four influenza A pandemics, where viruses have emerged from mammals or birds with the ability to transmit and cause disease in human populations. Since 2021, a high-pathogenicity strain of avian influenza, H5N1, has caused a panzootic (pandemic of animals), with global spread in wild birds, resulting in frequent spillovers into farmed poultry and into mammals, including mammal species not previously known to be affected by influenza A. This has created increased opportunity for reassortment, mutation, human infection, and potential adaptation to transmit. The risk to humans and the impact are difficult to quantify but of mounting concern to public health bodies. Here, we examine the risk of an H5N1 pandemic emerging and spreading in humans and the potential impact of an H5N1 pandemic.
n1b8d5ef8fc0a: Passive anti–amyloid-β immunotherapy has shifted from repeated phase 3 failure to reproducible, although modest, clinical slowing in biomarker-defined early Alzheimer's disease. We review lessons from first-generation antibodies, including inadequate target engagement, late-stage enrollment, and limited outcome sensitivity. We then compare second-generation agents (i.e., aducanumab, lecanemab, and donanemab) highlighting amyloid-β species selectivity, plaque clearance kinetics, and durability, and we discuss emerging delivery innovations. Safety is dominated by amyloid-related imaging abnormalities, likely reflecting cerebrovascular amyloid vulnerability, and requires timely baseline magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) screening; APOE -informed counseling; and standardized, front-loaded MRI surveillance with symptom-triggered evaluation. We summarize prevention trials in autosomal dominant and sporadic preclinical populations and consider prospects for combination or sequential regimens with tau-targeting therapies. Finally, we focus on biomarker-guided implementation: blood-based prescreening, confirmation pathways, monitoring of biological response, and treat-to-clear or stopping concepts, alongside unresolved issues of health-system readiness, equity, and budget impact. Registry-enabled learning is emphasized to generate real-world safety and effectiveness evidence.
n5d67d8c9fb69: Laboratory rats ( Rattus norvegicus ) have been invaluable to biomedical research and are well-suited for physiological analyses. Nevertheless, technical challenges in embryo and genetic manipulation have historically hindered the generation of genetically modified rats, thereby limiting their use for in vivo functional genetic studies. Recent advances, including genome editing and pluripotent/germline stem cell technologies, have substantially expanded rat genetic engineering. This review summarizes the historical background and recent advances in rat embryo manipulation and highlights the rapid development of genetic tools in rats, now catching up with those available in mice. These advances provide an opportunity to reassess the value of rats as experimental models. Furthermore, the combined use of mice and rats, exemplified by interspecific chimeras and comparative studies, offers new insights into conserved and species-specific physiological mechanisms across mammals.
n75b8f56767a0: Research on misinformation has expanded rapidly over the past decade. This review examines areas of consensus and contention within the literature on misinformation, with particular attention to conceptual definitions, measurement approaches, and theoretical explanations. We outline views on what it means to be susceptible to misinformation and advocate for assessing susceptibility by focusing on the ability to discern true from false claims. Although exposure to fake news is less common online than many think, we argue that misinformation—more broadly construed—continues to be a major problem. We review evidence on cognitive and socio-affective mechanisms underlying susceptibility to misinformation, including repetition effects, lack of analytic reasoning, political identity, and information environments. We also evaluate interventions such as fact-checking, prebunking, psychological inoculation, and accuracy prompts. Overall, the literature reveals several robust findings but also significant methodological limitations and theoretical disagreements that suggest fruitful future directions for misinformation research.
naa076d78042e: Ongoing liberalization and legalization of cannabis policy in the United States have shifted the focus of policy discussions to how legal markets should be regulated to protect public health. We reviewed the scientific literature on cannabis legalization, mapped current state cannabis policies using the National Conference of State Legislatures cannabis policy domains, and conducted a scoping review of peer-reviewed studies from 2015 to 2026 that measured specific cannabis policies and health or use outcomes. Across the 48 included studies, evidence was concentrated in licensing and business practices, nonmedical adult use regulations, medical program regulations, and local control. Our scoping review suggests that retail availability, outlet density, proximity, and local restrictions shape cannabis exposure and use. Evidence was limited for product regulations, taxes and revenue allocation, hemp/cannabidiol policies, justice system provisions, and public health/research policies. Future research should incorporate detailed policy coding, implementation measures, market data, surveillance data, and stronger researcher–policymaker linkages.
n81a52388c615: by Zhe Jiang Herein, we proposed a mild and effective approach for the surface modification of wool fiber using a natural deep eutectic solvent (NADES) composed of choline chloride and ascorbic acid (Vitamin C), avoiding the unsustainability of oxidation methods and severe damage of enzyme methods. The results showed that the NADES could remove keratin-associated proteins partly due to the breakage of disulfide bonds with the retention of the protein’s main macromolecular skeleton and secondary structure, and the exposure degree increase of hydrophilic groups. Furthermore, the hydrophily, dye performance, and anti-felting properties were improved and met industrial standards. The developed method had apparent advances in treatment time, energy consumption, and chemical usage compared to present methods. This work contributes to the further investigation of NADES on the protein modification.
nf7ecbbc3ffc0: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains the leading cause of death worldwide. While clinical scores provide modest predictive accuracy, the electrocardiogram (ECG) is rarely leveraged for prognosis. Artificial intelligence (AI) and deep learning now enable extraction of high-dimensional features from ECG waveforms for predicting cardiovascular outcomes. Our objective was to systematically evaluate the prognostic performance of AI-enabled ECG models for predicting all-cause mortality, cardiovascular mortality, and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). We searched PubMed, Cochrane CENTRAL, IEEE Xplore, and Google Scholar through November 2025 for studies using AI/ML models with 12-lead or single-lead ECGs to predict all-cause mortality, cardiovascular mortality, or MACE in adults (≥18 years old). Eligible studies included adults (≥18 years) using ECG as primary input. Two reviewers independently screened and extracted data. Narrative synthesis was conducted due to heterogeneity. Thirteen studies were included (~5.9 million patients). Eleven reported all-cause mortality (8 short-term: 30-day to 1-year), four reported cardiovascular mortality, and eight assessed MACE (4 composite MACE, 4 individual components). Models predominantly used convolutional neural networks [CNNs] on raw ECG waveforms. C-statistics ranged 0.70–0.89 for mortality prediction. Definitions and follow-up durations varied, limiting direct comparison. AI-ECG models demonstrate strong potential for predicting mortality and cardiovascular events with consistent performance and scalability. However, prospective validation and standardization are essential before clinical implementation.
n99035b192baf: Semantic segmentation of high-resolution remote sensing imagery in complex urban scenes often suffers from insufficient modeling of boundary neighborhoods, causing ambiguity near class interfaces and weakening the continuity of elongated structures. To address this issue, we propose a Boundary-Topology-Guided Structural Refinement Network (BTSR-Net). Built upon HRNet-OCR, BTSR-Net introduces a Geometric Boundary–Distance Branch (GBD) with joint boundary–distance supervision to capture spatial transitions around class boundaries, a Multi-scale Topology-Guided Structural Fusion (MTSF) module to enhance connectivity representation of elongated structures, and a dual-stream structural refinement mechanism to perform local residual correction within a boundary-distance-defined refinement narrow-band. Experiments on the ISPRS Potsdam and Vaihingen datasets demonstrate improvements in overall segmentation accuracy, boundary quality, and structural connectivity. On Potsdam, BTSR-Net achieves 84.70% mIoU, 43.17% mBIoU, and 81.63% clDice, exceeding the baseline by 2.91, 5.66, and 3.74 percentage points, respectively. On Vaihingen, it achieves 93.94% mIoU, 73.90% mBIoU, and 95.46% clDice, with corresponding improvements of 2.27, 9.39, and 2.12 percentage points. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of BTSR-Net for structure-sensitive semantic segmentation in high-resolution remote sensing imagery.
n42853ef1ff59: Early-stage defects in wind turbine bearings often generate weak impulsive signatures that are easily obscured by strong background noise, posing a significant challenge to accurate extraction of fault-related features. To overcome this limitation, a novel concave sparsity-assisted time-reassigned multisynchrosqueezing transform (CSA-TMSST) is developed to improve the extraction of weak fault-related signatures. First, a non-convex sparse optimization model incorporating the generalized minimax-concave (GMC) penalty is established to reconstruct fault impulsive components from the raw signal. The introduced GMC-based sparse regularization enhances signal sparsity, enabling the accurate extraction of impulsive fault signatures. Subsequently, TMSST is employed to characterize the reconstructed signal in the time-frequency (TF) domain, yielding a more concentrated time-frequency representation (TFR). Furthermore, the iterative reassignment mechanism is utilized to enhance the concentration of TF energy distribution, thereby yielding a clearer TFR of transient fault features. Finally, characteristic fault frequencies are identified via spectral analysis. The results demonstrate that CSA-TMSST is capable of extracting weak fault-related signatures and producing high-quality TFRs under strong noise conditions, confirming its effectiveness and superiority.
n2870d1b32540: by Hafez Mohammad Nazmul Ahsan, Shaheera Rahman, Labida Islam, Monjur Rahman, Farhana Zaman, Rowshan Ara, Hossain Mohammed Omar Khayum, Saidur Rahman Mashreky

n1e32ecdf9aa7: Objective To address the occupational exposure risks caused by instantaneous steam overflow when opening the top cover of hatch-type boiling disinfectors in the central sterile supply department, this study developed an interlocked centrifugal exhaust system (ICES) characterized by operational simplicity and high adaptability. Methods The ICES was assembled using a centrifugal fan, Hall effect switch, instant relay, time-delay relay, solid-state relay, and piping. The system achieved automatic start/stop of the fan based on the open‑or‑closed status of the top cover. A self-controlled design was adopted on one hatch-type boiling disinfector. Temperature was measured at the chamber edge (T1) and at the technician’s facial position (T2). Airborne particle counts were also measured at the technician’s facial position. Measurements were performed under conditions with and without the ICES enabled. Data were analyzed using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test. Results After enabling the ICES, T1 and T2 decreased by 20.89% and 31.31%, respectively. The median temperature at T2 was 21.5 °C, which was close to the ambient temperature. The reduction ratios for airborne particle counts of six different sizes at the technician’s facial position ranged from 53.09% to 67.83%. All differences between groups were statistically significant (all P < 0.001). Conclusion The ICES effectively reduces steam overflow upon the top-cover opening of hatch-type boiling disinfectors and lowers the risk of occupational injury. With advantages such as wide installation adaptability, imperceptible operation, and convenient maintenance, it provides a stable and reliable solution for the safety retrofitting of existing hatch-type boiling disinfectors.
n5ec6600fc50b: The economic valuation of ecosystem services in agriculture and agroforestry is crucial for sustainable development. However, valuation methods vary significantly across contexts. Using the PRISMA framework, we systematically reviewed 146 studies, combined effect sizes through meta-analytic modeling, and conducted spatial autocorrelation analyses to explore geographic patterns. Market price valuation (MPV) and contingent valuation (CVM) are the most used methods in ecosystem service assessments, accounting for 25.8% and 20.8% of studies, respectively. The CVM and life cycle impact assessment (LCIA) approaches play a key role in interdisciplinary research, connecting all ecosystem service categories. Analysis revealed extreme heterogeneity and significant publication bias for cultural (CULT), provisioning (PROV), and regulating (REG) services. Valuation outcomes are strongly influenced by the choice of methods (such as MPV and benefit transfer methods) and unit standardization practices, with effect sizes decreasing when values are standardized to United States dollars per ha per year (USD/ha/year). Spatial autocorrelation was minimal, indicating the importance of local context in the valuation results. Temporal trends indicate episodic changes in the relative effectiveness of valuation approaches. Empirically, MPV showed greater robustness (18%) than CVM, which exhibited greater sensitivity to data constraints (16%). These findings highlight the need to prioritize data quality and context specificity within standardized valuation frameworks to improve policy relevance and comparability in ecosystem service assessments, particularly for underrepresented CULT and supporting (SUP) services.
n143dedc0c638: Cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) is a precursor to cervical cancer, and early detection of residual or recurrent disease is therefore critical for effective management. This study evaluated whether HPV E6/E7 mRNA status predicts recurrence in patients with CIN who underwent loop electrosurgical excision procedure (LEEP). People’s Hospital of Nanning between January 2019 and July 2022 were included. Patients who underwent LEEP for high-grade cervical lesions at the First Follow-up commenced 4–6 months after LEEP and continued for 24 months; abnormal findings during this period prompted referral for colposcopy or cervical biopsy. Of the 91 patients, 3 (3.30%) experienced recurrence within 24 months. Recurrence rates were similar between patients with preoperative E6/E7 mRNA positivity (3.23%) and negativity (3.45%) (p = 0.956), and between postoperative E6/E7 mRNA status groups (5.26% in the negative group vs. 0% in the positive group; p = 0.814). Although 66.7% of patients shifted from positive to negative E6/E7 mRNA status after LEEP (p < 0.001), this change was not associated with recurrence risk. Preoperative E6/E7 mRNA yielded a sensitivity of 66.67% and specificity of 31.82%, whereas postoperative E6/E7 mRNA showed a sensitivity of 0% and specificity of 97.30%. In conclusion, E6/E7 mRNA status before and after LEEP did not predict recurrence in patients with CIN. Despite a significant reduction in E6/E7 mRNA positivity after surgery, its low sensitivity underscores the need for more effective biomarkers in follow-up care.
n78b79160d5fb: Pregnancy is accompanied by substantial physiological adaptations that may alter maternal micronutrient concentrations. A prospective longitudinal pregnancy-neonatal cohort of 51 healthy pregnant women was established at 6–8 weeks of gestation in Lianyungang, Jiangsu, China, confirmed by fetal heart and bud on B-ultrasound. Pregnancy complications, outcomes, and neonatal health at day 42 were confirmed. Forty-three women who completed all assessments and had uncomplicated pregnancies with favorable maternal and neonatal outcomes were included in the final analysis. Whole-blood trace elements and serum vitamins were quantified during the first trimester (12.3 ± 0.9 weeks), second trimester (25.6 ± 1.2 weeks), and third trimester (32.7 ± 2.3 weeks) using ICP-MS and UHPLC-MS/MS. The results showed that copper, calcium, and vitamin D peaked in the second trimester, whereas iron, zinc, magnesium, and lead reached their nadir in the second trimester. Meanwhile, manganese and vitamins E and K increased progressively throughout gestation. In contrast, several B vitamins showed an overall downward trend, while vitamin B12 remained relatively stable. These findings demonstrate clear trimester-specific changes in maternal micronutrient levels during healthy pregnancy. Given the relatively small sample size, these longitudinal data provide preliminary evidence to inform the establishment of region-specific and trimester-specific reference intervals and deficiency thresholds for micronutrients in healthy pregnant women.
n41517052c522: In humans, the membrane-bound serine protease prostasin encoded by Prss8 is associated with preeclampsia, a gestational hypertension disorder affecting blood supply of the placenta. Deficiency of Prss8 in mice resulted in embryonic lethality by embryonic day (E) 14.5 and impaired maturation of placental labyrinth. We found in Prss8-/- embryos at E11.5 and E12.5 a reduced frequency of both circulating primitive and erythro-myeloid progenitor (EMP)-derived definitive erythroblasts in the yolk sac, placenta and fetal liver. Single-cell RNA sequencing analyses revealed a downregulation of fetal hemoglobin genes and an upregulation of ribosomal genes in primitive erythroid cells of Prss8-/- embryos, indicating a defective erythroid maturation. We suggest that prostasin regulates primitive erythropoiesis in a cell-extrinsic manner, since its expression was absent in circulating erythroid cells. Indeed, the yolk sac vascular remodeling of Prss8-/- embryos was impaired as evidenced by reduced vessel branching and junctions, likely affecting placenta vascularization and contributing to embryonic demise. Our findings unveil a novel role for prostasin during developmental erythropoiesis and vascular patterning and provide insight into how Prss8 dysregulation may contribute to placental pathologies such as preeclampsia.
n9002ff067bbc: Introduction Mitochondrial dysfunction is central to type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) pathogenesis, driving insulin resistance and pancreatic β-cell dysfunction. Age-related mitochondrial impairment worsens this in older adults, yet evidence on mitochondrial interventions for this group is limited. This protocol outlines a systematic review and conditional network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials evaluating mitochondrial interventions in adults aged 60+ with T2DM. Objective The primary objective of this systematic review and conditional network meta-analysis (NMA) is to evaluate the comparative efficacy and safety of diverse mitochondrial-related interventions, including pharmacological agents, nutritional supplements, and lifestyle modifications, relative to placebo, standard care, or no intervention, on mitochondrial function biomarkers in adults aged 60 years or older with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Interventions with mitochondrial effects are operationally defined as those whose primary mechanism is known to target mitochondrial pathways or those that are explicitly evaluated for their effects on direct markers of mitochondrial function in the trial.The secondary objectives are: (1) to assess the impact of these interventions on glycemic and metabolic control outcomes including glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c), fasting plasma glucose (FPG), fasting insulin, homeostatic model assessment of insulin resistance (HOMA-IR), body weight, and body mass index (BMI); (2) to conduct a conditional NMA to compare and rank the relative efficacy of different intervention categories if the evidence network is sufficiently connected and clinically coherent; and (3) to explore potential sources of heterogeneity (e.g., intervention duration, baseline HbA1c levels) via prespecified subgroup and sensitivity analyses. Methods and analysis Prepared per PRISMA-P, the review will follow PRISMA 2020 and PRISMA-NMA if applicable. Registered with PROSPERO (ID: CRD420251145356), searches will cover PubMed, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, Web of Science, and Scopus from inception to April 2026. Focused on T2DM, mitochondrial function/dysfunction, and interventions, age eligibility will be assessed during full-text screening. Primary analysis includes trials with participants aged 60+ or extractable data for this group; sensitivity analyses will include those with mean/median age ≥ 60. Two reviewers will handle screening, data extraction, and bias assessment using RoB 2.Analysis will focus on trials reporting mitochondrial function outcomes, categorized by biological domain, tissue source, and assay method. Glycemic control, geriatric health, and safety are secondary outcomes. Network meta-analysis will be conducted if a connected evidence network exists; otherwise, pairwise meta-analysis or narrative synthesis will be used. Random-effects models will be employed, with heterogeneity assessed via subgroup analysis and meta-regression. If significant heterogeneity persists, a Synthesis Without Meta-Analysis (SWiM) framework narrative review will be done. Evidence certainty will be appraised using GRADE and CINeMA. Ethics and dissemination Ethics approval is not required for this systematic review as the systematic review will include only previously anonymised data from primary studies. Dissemination of the findings of the final systematic review will occur through publishing in a peer-reviewed journal. PROSPERO registration number CRD420251145356
nefc710efff63: Background Family physicians provide most outpatient care in patients’ last year of life, but it remains unclear how geographic distance between patients and their physicians affects continuity of care. Patients living farther from care providers may experience reduced access and more fragmented care. This study examined whether geographic proximity to a family physician is associated with relational continuity of outpatient care in the last year of life. Methods We conducted a population‑level retrospective cohort study of adults who died in Ontario, Canada, from 2021 to 2024, using linked health administrative data. Geographic proximity was measured using quartiles of the shortest driving distance (km) between each patient’s residence and their family physician’s practice location. Relational continuity was assessed using established measures capturing the concentration of visits, dispersion of care across physicians, and the temporal regularity of visits. Associations were estimated using proportional‑odds regression models adjusted for demographic, socioeconomic, and clinical factors. Results Among 400,499 patients, the mean age at death was 76.0 years, 52.2% were male, the mean (SD) distance to their family physician was 25.5 (92.0) km, with the highest quartile residing more than 14.2 km away from their family physician. Greater distance was associated with modestly lower relational continuity: each one-quartile increase in distance was linked to lower odds of higher continuity with the usual family physician (cOR: 0.88, 95%CI: 0.87, 0.88). Sensitivity analyses using travel time and Euclidean distance produced consistent findings. Discussion Geographic proximity is a significant determinant of outpatient continuity near the end of life. Patients living farther from their family physicians experience more fragmented care, underscoring the need for system-level strategies to reduce geographic barriers, including improved local access to primary care and enhanced virtual-care models.
nd839d66524ca: by Sungbae Jo This cross-sectional secondary analysis examined medical rehabilitation use and regional bypass among Korean children and adolescents with registered disabilities, using a two-stage access framework that distinguished entry into medical-institution rehabilitation from out-of-region use after entry. We analyzed public-use data from the 2023 National Survey on Persons with Disabilities, restricting the sample to respondents younger than 19 years (n = 399; weighted national estimate, 88,611). Weighted descriptive statistics and modified Poisson regression with robust standard errors were used to estimate prevalence ratios (PRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Overall, 50.0% had no medical-institution rehabilitation use, 31.5% used in-region rehabilitation, and 18.6% used out-of-region rehabilitation; among rehabilitation users, 37.1% reported out-of-region care. In stage 1, non-developmental disability type was associated with higher medical rehabilitation use (PR, 1.61; 95% CI, 1.28–2.03), whereas eup/myeon residence was associated with lower use (PR, 0.66; 95% CI, 0.46–0.94). In stage 2, province residence (PR, 2.13; 95% CI, 1.38–3.27) and non-developmental disability type (PR, 1.74; 95% CI, 1.13–2.69) were associated with out-of-region use, while male sex was associated with lower out-of-region use (PR, 0.62; 95% CI, 0.42–0.92). The most common reason for non-use was use of non-medical facilities (27.4%); better treatment and absence of nearby medical institutions were leading reasons for out-of-region care. Pediatric medical rehabilitation access involves challenges to both non-use and out-of-region use, with implications for local entry support, regional capacity-building, and cross-sector service integration.
n40a110658caa: In situ glia-to-neuron conversion induced by a single transcription factor is a promising regenerative strategy for treating central nervous system injuries and neurodegenerative diseases. Previous studies reported that NeuroD1 can induce microglia-to-neuron cross-lineage conversion and improve recovery after brain injury. However, these findings remain controversial. To examine the ability of NeuroD1 in inducing microglia-to-neuron conversion, we employed virus-free genetic lineage-tracing systems in mice to specifically induce NeuroD1 expression in microglia and track the cell fate of NeuroD1-expressing cells at multiple timepoints. Meanwhile, we longitudinally monitored NeuroD1-expressing microglia via two-photon imaging and characterized their transcriptional profile by single-cell RNA sequencing. All observations across these methods revealed that NeuroD1-expressing cells retained their microglia identity and cannot convert into neurons, no matter under physiological and injury conditions. Instead, sustained expression of NeuroD1 facilitated microglia apoptosis in vivo. Collectively, our findings provide strong evidence that NeuroD1 alone is not sufficient to induce microglia-to-neuron conversion. This study further highlights the importance of rigorous lineage-tracing and cell fate-mapping strategies for validating in situ glia-to-neuron conversion.
n315bae484e0e: Two evolutionary highly conserved functions of dopamine are to carry ‘teaching’ signals during associative learning and to control movement. In mammals and humans, these functions are generally thought to be produced by different populations of neurons.
